item.title: Goal-Holding Agents Under Budget Guards: Pre- and Post-Fix Overspend Audit and Replication Limits
item.dc:creator: Open Interface Engineering
item.description: Pre-fix (36/5,400 overspends) and post-fix (0/10,800 overspends) budget-guard experiments across 30 Sudoku tasks, fired falsifiers (R-F1..R-F6), non-replicating tight-budget gains, and on-chip reported_j limits.
item.content:encoded:
Pre-fix (36/5,400 overspends) and post-fix (0/10,800 overspends) budget-guard experiments across 30 Sudoku tasks, fired falsifiers (R-F1..R-F6), non-replicating tight-budget gains, and on-chip reported_j limits.

Signed Provenance · Self-Checked (human_in_gate = false; automated build, benchmark, and proof-checking scripts ran without manual override — not externally peer-reviewed; see Verification & AI-Use Disclosure and Epistemic Glossary).

Canonical Post-Review Essay (rel="canonical"): https://blog.openie.dev/posts/agency/

Primary Research Paper: https://research.openie.dev/papers/agency/

1-Command Replication Kit: https://github.com/openIE-dev/openie-research-experiments/tree/main/replicate · Study Repository: https://github.com/openIE-dev/openie-research-experiments

Canonical Artifact ID: blake3:tv:7da82d901b877b47d94327d99418d995f9ba998d898a17a75f32efebd8f3708f · Evidence Tags: [E] · [M] · [S] · Telemetry Class: reported_j

Primary-paper summary: pre-fix (36/5,400) vs. post-fix (0/10,800) budget-guard audit, fired falsifiers R-F1..R-F6, and non-replicating tight-budget gains (reported_j). Dedicated to the public domain under CC0-1.0.

Key Claims & Audited Scope ([T] / [E] / [M] / [S])

  1. [E · reported_j, Darwin ri_energy_nj & Linux RAPL] Before fixing the guard boundary, 36 of 5,400 episodes overspent their declared budget in exploratory Run 1 (firing falsifier R-F2); moving goal comparison and receipt logging inside the guard reduced overspends to 0 of 10,800 episodes (0/5,400 per half) in preregistered Run 2 and Machine 2 Part B cycle accounting, whereas Machine 2 Part A raw Linux RAPL per-act checks recorded 320–327 overspends per condition because 0.04 ms acts fell below ~1 ms RAPL counter update granularity.
  2. [E · Negative Result & Fired Falsifiers] Exploratory Run 1 showed +2.65 extra closed Sudoku tasks at tight budget B = 1.0, but that tight-budget gain did not replicate in preregistered Run 2 or on Machine 2 (shared-task joules were statistically indistinguishable, and only loose-budget B = 2.0 closure +2.8 / +0.825 tasks replicated); falsifiers R-F1 (guard overhead), R-F4 (cross-machine ranking reversal Kendall tau-b = -0.037), R-F5 (CV > 0.25 on unquiesced hosts), and R-F6 (integrated derivative mismatch) also fired.
  3. [M · Unit Positivity, Not Tight Hardware Floor] Comparing macro-CPU episode joules (3.6 × 10^14 to 5.0 × 10^15 times k_B T ln 2) against Landauer bit-erasure checks bookkeeping sign positivity (R-F7), not tight operational proximity to physical thermodynamic limits on out-of-order processors.

Methods, Baselines, Sample Sizes (N) & Licensing Scope

  • Hardware & Telemetry: Machine 1: Apple Silicon macOS (proc_pid_rusage ri_energy_nj L3 reported_j). Machine 2: x86-64 Linux (powercap intel-rapl package counter L2 reported_j in Part A; calibrated cycle counter in Part B). Unquiesced hosts (quiet_window = no); no external DC shunt or AC wall meter (measured_j = null).
  • Workload & Suite: 30 bounded constraint-propagation and backtracking Sudoku episodes evaluated across 3 budget levels (B = 0.5, 1.0, 2.0 normalized units).
  • Baselines Compared: Three internal controller arms: adaptive tempo/cascade (sigma-selector), fixed heuristic cascade, and goal-blind unguarded loop. External LLM/solver baselines: not benchmarked in this study.
  • Runs (N) & Uncertainty / Spread: Run 1: N = 5,400 episodes (20 seeds × 3 arms × 3 budgets × 30 tasks). Preregistered Run 2: N = 10,800 episodes (40 seeds, split into two 5,400-episode halves). Machine 2: N = 10,800 episodes per part. Episode energy CV > 0.25 at binding budgets (R-F5 fired).
  • Cold vs. Warm Caching Scope: Stateless per-episode solver resets (0 cross-episode solution memoization); OS page cache warm across sequential seeds.
  • Artifact & License Status: Primary manuscript and falsifier tables public (CC0-1.0); experiment summaries in openIE-dev/openie-research-experiments (Apache-2.0, self-checked, externally unreproduced).

Problem, Scope & Framing Qualifiers

The primary paper defines an engineered goal-holding agent operationally as a control loop maintaining a target predicate under an explicit energy budget [M]. Earlier blog summaries compressed a heavily qualified, self-critical manuscript into sweeping thermodynamic slogans. In reality, modern out-of-order CPUs operate 14 to 15 orders of magnitude above k_B T ln 2 (3.6 × 10^14 to 5.0 × 10^15 times the 300 K Landauer floor in these runs) [E]. Referencing Landauer in the formal model serves strictly to enforce positive physical units (e_act > 0, falsifier R-F7), not to claim that high-level software schedulers approach physical bit-erasure limits [M].

Mechanism, Experimental Results & Guard Fix

The experimental harness compares three internal control arms (sigma-selector adaptive routing, fixed cascade, and goal-blind baseline) across 30 Sudoku constraint tasks at three budget caps (B = 0.5, 1.0, 2.0) [E]. A central engineering lesson came from an accounting bug caught between Run 1 and Run 2:

  • Exploratory Run 1 (Pre-Fix, N = 5,400 episodes): Goal-comparison and receipt-emission costs executed after the pre-act budget check. As a result, 36 of 5,400 episodes overspent their cap (9 sigma-selector and 7 fixed-cascade episodes at B = 1.0, plus 20 goal-blind episodes at B = 0.5), firing falsifier R-F2 [E].
  • Preregistered Run 2 (Post-Fix, N = 10,800 episodes across two 5,400-episode halves): Reserving worst-case comparison plus receipt cost inside the guard before committing an act reduced overspends to 0 of 10,800 episodes (0/5,400 in each half; 95% Clopper–Pearson upper bound <= 3.42 × 10^-4 per episode under the tested workload) on Darwin ri_energy_nj and Machine 2 Part B cycle accounting [E].
  • Sub-Millisecond Counter Aliasing (Machine 2 Part A): When the guard instead polled raw Linux RAPL package counters directly on ~0.04 ms solver acts, RAPL updated only every ~1 ms ([S], Khan et al., 2018), letting dozens of unbilled micro-acts slip past stale readings and causing 320 to 327 overspends per condition [E].

Limitations, Negative Results & Fired Falsifiers

Unlike promotional summaries, the primary manuscript documents six fired falsifiers and a failed replication that narrow what this study supports [E]:

  • Tight-budget gain did not replicate: Run 1 suggested +2.65 additional solved tasks for sigma-selector at B = 1.0, but preregistered Run 2 and Machine 2 Part B showed no tight-budget advantage, and energy per solved task on mutually completed instances was equal (R-F3 fired in Run 1). Only the loose-budget (B = 2.0) closure gain (+2.8 tasks on Machine 1; +0.825 on Machine 2 Part B) replicated [E].
  • Cross-host ranking instability & host noise: Cross-substrate progress-per-joule rank correlation reversed on Machine 2 (Kendall tau-b = -0.037, firing R-F4), binding-budget coefficient of variation exceeded 0.25 (R-F5) because background OS daemons were not quiesced (quiet_window = no), guard bookkeeping overhead fired R-F1 on tiny steps, and integrated iota rankings diverged from mean J* (R-F6) [E].

Energy & Telemetry Scope

All energy readings in this study are operating-system or on-chip reported_j estimates (macOS proc_pid_rusage ri_energy_nj L3 and Linux powercap RAPL L2; measured_j = null, board_metered = false) [E]. Relative comparisons are valid only within the same host and counter channel on coarse multi-millisecond windows; fine-grained act accounting requires deterministic cycle/instruction budgets calibrated against external DC shunts rather than sub-millisecond RAPL polling [E].

Epistemic Non-Mixing & Telemetry Ledger

Open Interface Engineering enforces strict non-mixing across physical rail shunts, on-chip counters, datasheet models, and uninstrumented analyses (measured_j $\perp$ reported_j $\perp$ est_j $\perp$ unmetered — cross-class addition or direct cross-tier ratioing is blocked):

  • Provenance Gate: Signed Provenance · Self-Checked (human_in_gate = false)
  • Acquisition Tier: On-Chip Counter (reported_j)
  • Telemetry Disclosure: macOS Darwin ri_energy_nj L3 & Linux RAPL L2 on-chip counters; measured_j = null (no wall meter).
  • Evidence Class: reported_j (board_metered = false)
  • Catalog Anchor Reading: 0.085 J (reported_j)
  • Sensor / Formula Scope: Darwin ri_energy_nj L3 & calibrated Linux cycle/RAPL counters across Sudoku budget-guard episodes (measured_j = null)

Related Work & Primary Literature ([S])

  • Landauer (1961) & Bennett (1973): IBM J. Res. Dev. 5(3) and 17(6) — physical bit-erasure lower bounds (k_B T ln 2), cited strictly for unit positivity rather than macro-CPU operational floors [S].
  • Horowitz (ISSCC 2014) & Khan et al. (ACM TOMPECS 2018): Empirical silicon instruction/DRAM energy scales (pJ–nJ) and Linux RAPL ~1 ms update-interval and thermal-drift characterization [S].
  • Zeng et al. (ECOSystem, ASPLOS 2002) & Roy et al. (Cinder, EuroSys 2011): Operating-system currentcy/reserve/tap abstractions that precede per-episode agent budget guards [S].
  • Simon & Kadane (1975) & Russell & Wefald (1991): Satisficing search and bounded metareasoning under explicit computational cost constraints [S].
  • FrugalGPT (Chen, Zaharia & Zou, 2023) & RouteLLM (Ong et al., ICLR 2025): Cost-bounded multi-model routing cascades in modern language-model serving [S].

item.title: Metered Commit Gates: KV260 Whole-SOM Shunt Measurements, Statistical Safety Bounds, and Cascade Scope
item.dc:creator: Open Interface Engineering
item.description: Whole-SOM TI INA260 shunt power-slope readings on AMD Kria KV260 (11.43 nJ/cycle, N = 4 A/B/A passes), inconclusive 98 pJ seed delta near sensor floor, and Clopper-Pearson bounds over 209,261 simulated checks.
item.content:encoded:
Whole-SOM TI INA260 shunt power-slope readings on AMD Kria KV260 (11.43 nJ/cycle, N = 4 A/B/A passes), inconclusive 98 pJ seed delta near sensor floor, and Clopper-Pearson bounds over 209,261 simulated checks.

Signed Provenance · Self-Checked (human_in_gate = false; automated build, benchmark, and proof-checking scripts ran without manual override — not externally peer-reviewed; see Verification & AI-Use Disclosure and Epistemic Glossary).

Canonical Post-Review Essay (rel="canonical"): https://blog.openie.dev/posts/gates/

Primary Research Paper: https://research.openie.dev/papers/gates/

1-Command Replication Kit: https://github.com/openIE-dev/openie-research-experiments/tree/main/replicate · Study Repository: https://github.com/openIE-dev/mixture-of-limits

Canonical Artifact ID: blake3:tv:b6075421aa4a225d509d07481bc5a850f9e1dc14424cd92bd9abe3ebe93260a3 · Evidence Tags: [E] · [M] · [S] · Telemetry Class: measured_j

KV260 whole-SOM INA260 power-slope reading (11,428 pJ/cycle, SE = 129 pJ, measured_j), inconclusive 98 pJ seed delta, and 209,261-trial simulated gate audit. Dedicated to the public domain under CC0-1.0.

Key Claims & Audited Scope ([T] / [E] / [M] / [S])

  1. [E · measured_j, KV260 TI INA260 Whole-SOM Shunt] Stepping an 8-lane gate fabric at 25 MHz (2.4999 × 10^7 gate cycles/s, ~6.25 × 10^8 cycles per 25 s window) raised whole-module VCC_SOM power by +0.2857 W (SE = 0.0032 W across N = 4 interleaved A/B/A passes at ~4 Hz), yielding 11,428 pJ/cycle (11.43 nJ, SE = 129 pJ, or ~1.43 nJ per lane decision) across PS + PL + DDR + regulators combined—whereas a 98.0 pJ (SE = 30.8 pJ, +0.0098 W ≈ 1.96 mA at 5 V) seed-fabric delta sits near the INA260 1.25 mA current step and is explicitly inconclusive.
  2. [E/M · Simulated Safety Gate Bound] Across 209,261 simulated inverted-pendulum states (21^3 = 9,261 grid + 200,000 near-threshold Monte Carlo samples against Vdot <= epsilon), the gate recorded 0 observed false allows in 209,261 simulated trials (95% Clopper–Pearson upper bound <= 1.43 × 10^-5, ~1.4 per 100,000, under the tested state generator, with 79/209,261 = 0.038% conservative false refusals; grid/Monte Carlo simulation cannot prove universal absence of bugs).
  3. [M · Cold vs. Assumed Zipf Caching] The reported 16.7x frontier-call reduction in the Mixture-of-Limits (MoL) cascade comes from an assumed stationary Zipf(s = 1.1) repeat-arrival stream where verified answers memoize into exact lookup; on all-novel cold arrivals, cache reuse is 1.0x (zero call savings), and cached entries must be invalidated whenever specifications change.

Methods, Baselines, Sample Sizes (N) & Licensing Scope

  • Hardware & Telemetry: Hardware rung: AMD Kria KV260 (XCK26 UltraScale+ SOM) instrumented via onboard TI INA260 I2C shunt across whole-module VCC_SOM (5.04 V rail; 1.25 mA current LSB, 5 mA max offset, 0.15% gain error; measured_j). Software simulations (NI-1..NI-4, MoL Zipf curves): analytical op-counters and Python/Rust simulation (est_j / [M]).
  • Workload & Suite: KV260: 25 MHz 8-lane pipelined LUT/comparator commit-gate fabric (~6.25 × 10^8 cycles per 25 s window). Software: 209,261 discrete pendulum Lyapunov (Vdot) and Control Barrier Function (CBF) checks (NI-1..NI-4) plus synthetic Zipf(s = 1.1) cascade streams.
  • Baselines Compared: KV260: halted-clock vs. free-running 25 MHz gate fabric on the same SOM (A/B/A difference). Software: unguarded actuator pass-through and always-frontier single-tier invocation.
  • Runs (N) & Uncertainty / Spread: KV260 INA260: N = 4 interleaved A/B/A passes (15 s thermal settle + 25 s sampling at ~4 Hz ≈ 100 readings/window), mean 11,428 pJ/cycle, SE = 129 pJ (+0.2857 W, SE = 0.0032 W); seed-fabric delta 98.0 pJ, SE = 30.8 pJ (inconclusive near 1.25 mA LSB). Pendulum simulation: N = 209,261 deterministic states (95% Clopper–Pearson UB <= 1.43 × 10^-5).
  • Cold vs. Warm Caching Scope: Hardware gate is stateless combinational/pipelined (0 cache). Software MoL cascade separates cold first-exposure misses (0% hit rate) from warm Zipf(s = 1.1) memoized hits (16.7x call reduction only under stationary task repetition; requires hash invalidation on spec edits).
  • Artifact & License Status: Manuscript and CSV logs (CC0-1.0); openIE-dev/mixture-of-limits (Apache-2.0); KV260 bitstream/bench scripts self-checked by OpenIE, not externally replicated.

Problem, Scope & Sensor Boundary

A commit gate interposes a fast, deterministic admissibility check between an untrusted proposer and an irreversible state change [M]. Earlier blog headlines presented 11.43 nJ and zero bad commits without naming the whole-module rail boundary, sensor quantization step, or finite-sample statistical bound. Grounding directly in src/content/papers/gates.md restores all three engineering qualifiers [E].

KV260 Whole-SOM Shunt Measurement & Pendulum Simulation

  • Whole-SOM INA260 power-slope protocol [E, measured_j]: On AMD Kria KV260, the onboard TI INA260 sits on VCC_SOM (~5.04 V), metering the entire System-on-Module (ARM Cortex-A53 PS, UltraScale+ PL fabric, DDR4 memory, and DC-DC regulators) rather than an isolated core LUT rail. Across N = 4 interleaved A/B/A halt-vs-run passes (15 s settle, 25 s capture at ~4 Hz while stepping 2.4999 × 10^7 8-lane cycles/s = ~6.25 × 10^8 cycles/window), active clocking added +0.2857 W (SE = 0.0032 W), giving 11,428 pJ/cycle (11.43 nJ, SE = 129 pJ, or ~1.43 nJ/lane) [E].
  • Inconclusive sub-LSB seed delta [E]: Comparing two internal LUT seed configurations shifted VCC_SOM power by only +0.0098 W (98.0 pJ/cycle, SE = 30.8 pJ), or ~1.96 mA at 5 V—barely 1.5x the INA260 1.25 mA ADC step (5 mA max offset). The primary paper therefore classifies the 98 pJ isolated-logic estimate as inconclusive without a dedicated low-ohm core-rail shunt [E].
  • Simulated Lyapunov/CBF gate (209,261 states) [E, M]: Evaluating quantized integer gate checks over 9,261 uniform grid points (21^3) plus 200,000 boundary-concentrated Monte Carlo draws produced 0 observed false allows in 209,261 simulated trials (95% Clopper–Pearson upper bound <= 1.43 × 10^-5, ~1.4 per 100,000, under the tested fault generator; fuzzing/simulation cannot prove absence of bugs) and 79 (0.038%) conservative boundary refusals caused by fixed-point guard margins [E].

Limitations, Predicate Disagreement (NI-4) & Caching Scope

  • Different safety predicates admit different actions (NI-4) [E]: In experiment NI-4, comparing a port-Hamiltonian passivity gate (lut_and_safe_ph: 0 Vdot violations, 4 barrier h < 0 excursions) against a Control Barrier Function set-invariance gate (cbf_energy_set: 0 h < 0 excursions, 3 Vdot spikes) showed explicit disagreement—proving that a gate enforces only the exact mathematical predicate encoded, not generic physical safety [E].
  • Zipfian memoization vs. cold generalization [M]: The MoL software simulation (16.7x fewer frontier model invocations) models an idealized Zipf(s = 1.1) workload where identical canonicalized tasks recur frequently. On strictly unique cold inputs, the lookup rung misses 100% of the time and adds gate-check overhead [M].

Energy & Telemetry Scope

Only the KV260 VCC_SOM INA260 reading (11.43 nJ/cycle) carries measured_j status; software OpCounter constants in the paper (such as placeholder 1 pJ LUT weights) are est_j analytical weights explicitly excluded from hardware claims [E, M]. Relative to a ~50–100 J workstation LLM call (reported_j in companion studies), a microsecond-scale deterministic gate check is orders of magnitude smaller, though cross-tier (measured_j vs reported_j) numbers are never ratioed directly (measured_j ⊥ reported_j).

Epistemic Non-Mixing & Telemetry Ledger

Open Interface Engineering enforces strict non-mixing across physical rail shunts, on-chip counters, datasheet models, and uninstrumented analyses (measured_j $\perp$ reported_j $\perp$ est_j $\perp$ unmetered — cross-class addition or direct cross-tier ratioing is blocked):

  • Provenance Gate: Signed Provenance · Self-Checked (human_in_gate = false)
  • Acquisition Tier: Whole-SOM DC Shunt (measured_j)
  • Telemetry Disclosure: AMD Kria KV260 whole-SOM VCC_SOM TI INA260 shunt (11.43 nJ/cycle, N=4 passes); 98 pJ seed delta inconclusive near 1.25 mA LSB.
  • Evidence Class: measured_j (board_metered = true)
  • Catalog Anchor Reading: 1.1428e-08 J (measured_j)
  • Sensor / Formula Scope: AMD Kria KV260 whole-SOM VCC_SOM TI INA260 halt-vs-run power-slope shunt (11,428 pJ/cycle, SE = 129 pJ, N = 4 passes at 25 MHz)

Related Work & Primary Literature ([S])

  • Ames et al. (IEEE TAC, 2017) & Ortega et al. (Automatica, 2002): Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) and port-Hamiltonian passivity for safety-critical control [S].
  • Simplex Architecture (Sha, IEEE Software 2001): Runtime assurance switching between high-performance untrusted controllers and verified safety envelopes [S].
  • FrugalGPT (Chen et al., 2023) & RouteLLM (Ong et al., ICLR 2025): Multi-tier LLM cascades trading cheap routing steps against frontier model calls [S].
  • Umuroglu et al. (LogicNets, FPL 2020): Quantized LUT-fabric inference on Xilinx FPGAs [S].

item.description: Evaluates a 5-language zero-model deterministic baseline (Shape D: N0/N1) committed via OpenTimestamps and drand against 6 LLMs across 4,030 instances and 6 upstream SWE-bench Verified repos.
item.content:encoded:
Evaluates a 5-language zero-model deterministic baseline (Shape D: N0/N1) committed via OpenTimestamps and drand against 6 LLMs across 4,030 instances and 6 upstream SWE-bench Verified repos.

Signed Provenance · Self-Checked (human_in_gate = false; automated build, benchmark, and proof-checking scripts ran without manual override — not externally peer-reviewed; see Verification & AI-Use Disclosure and Epistemic Glossary).

Canonical Post-Review Essay (rel="canonical"): https://blog.openie.dev/posts/deterministic-null/

Primary Research Paper: https://research.openie.dev/papers/deterministic-null/

1-Command Replication Kit: https://github.com/openIE-dev/openie-research-experiments/tree/main/replicate · Study Repository: https://github.com/openIE-dev/deterministic-null

Canonical Artifact ID: blake3:tv:d3018098f6b08132cb47527bca323e5c8236e9193f1375feffa9ebd20c21305c · Evidence Tags: [E] · [M] · [S] · Telemetry Class: reported_j

Hash-precommitted zero-model deterministic baseline vs. 6 LLMs across 4,030 instances and 6 SWE-bench Verified repos (openIE-dev/deterministic-null, Apache-2.0). Dedicated to the public domain under CC0-1.0.

Key Claims & Audited Scope ([T] / [E] / [M] / [S])

  1. [E · Hash-Precommitted Zero-Model Baseline] Shape D (strict N0 exact hash lookup + dev-crystallized N1 nearest-token retrieval, implemented bit-identically in Rust, C++20, Go, Julia, and Python) locked its lookup-store digest and evaluation seeds before test scoring using OpenTimestamps Bitcoin Calendar proofs and League of Entropy drand rounds 6663734 and 6664089—providing a hash-precommitted lookup store (not an external peer-reviewed clinical registry).
  2. [E · Cold Open Generalization vs. Bounded Templates] Across all 6 core models (Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, OpenAI gpt-oss-120b, xAI Grok 4.20, Alibaba Qwen 3.6 35B-A3B, and Google Gemma 4 E4B-it), single-turn prompts failed to beat Shape D on 9 of 10 bounded Track-A template cells (N = 2,840, where post-run audit noted K_eff = 6–12 template saturation), whereas on unique external public suites (N = 1,190: BFCL v3, tau-bench Retail, BigCodeBench v0.1.3, SWE-bench Verified localization) LLMs led by +45.83 to +95.00 percentage points, and on 6 real upstream SWE-bench Verified repos cold Shape D solved 0/6 while Opus 5.5 solved 5/6 (Sonnet 5.5 4/6, Grok 4.20 1/6).
  3. [E · Exact Recall vs. Generalization (reported_j)] Replaying the 5/6 verified SWE-bench patches at t = 2 (0 LLM calls) demonstrates exact hash-addressed recall, not unseen bug generalization, and invalidates whenever repo commits or test specs change; on a 600-request Zipf(s = 0.85) stream over 220 BigCodeBench tasks, online verified crystallization cut model calls and local reported_j by 3.59x (167 vs. 600 calls).

Methods, Baselines, Sample Sizes (N) & Licensing Scope

  • Hardware & Telemetry: Local models (Qwen 3.6 35B-A3B, Gemma 4 E4B-it) and Shape D (DNULLMM1) instrumented on Apple M5 Max (128 GB, macOS Darwin ri_energy_nj L3 reported_j; board_metered = false, measured_j = null). Cloud API models (Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, gpt-oss-120b, Grok 4.20) have reported_j = null (token/USD cost logged).
  • Workload & Suite: 4,030 held-out instances (2,840 Track-A bounded formal/structured instances across 10 cells + 1,190 Track-B unique public instances across BFCL v3, tau-bench Retail, BigCodeBench v0.1.3, and SWE-bench Verified 12-way localization) plus 6 full upstream SWE-bench Verified git repositories (psf/requests-5414, pytest-dev/pytest-10051, pytest-dev/pytest-10356, mwaskom/seaborn-3069, sympy/sympy-23824, sympy/sympy-17655).
  • Baselines Compared: Zero-model deterministic baseline (Shape D: N0 exact FNV-1a/SHA-256 lookup and N1 dev-split bigram/Jaccard nearest template) plus classical CDCL+DRAT SAT solver B1 on unique_3sat_drat, compared against 6 LLMs (plus DeepSeek V4 Flash, Qwen 3.8 Max, and Gemini 2.5 Flash in exp-002/exp-003 probes).
  • Runs (N) & Uncertainty / Spread: N = 4,030 paired per-item McNemar/exact binomial comparisons (p < 10^-6 on Track-B +45.83 to +95.00 pp increments); N = 6 full repo patch evaluations; N = 600 Zipf(0.85) online requests. Single deterministic greedy (temp = 0) pass per model-item cell (multi-temperature sampling variance not recorded).
  • Cold vs. Warm Caching Scope: Strictly separated: Track-B and t = 1 SWE-bench measure cold zero-hit novelty (0/6 Shape D, +60.00 pp BFCL v3, +95.00 pp BigCodeBench); t = 2 replay (5/6) and Zipf(0.85) (3.59x call cut) measure warm verified recall keyed by exact task/tree digest (stale immediately upon spec or AST change).
  • Artifact & License Status: Apache-2.0 public replication kit at https://github.com/openIE-dev/deterministic-null (all 5 languages + drand/OpenTimestamps proofs); self-checked by OpenIE, ready for external replication.

Problem, Terminology Corrections & Hash-Precommitment Scope

Two terminology clarifications address critiques of the earlier blog summary. First, we refer to Shape D directly as a zero-model deterministic baseline rather than clinical "placebo" metaphors: Shape D executes zero neural weights, pairing N0 (exact canonical input digest lookup) with N1 (deterministic token-overlap template selection from a frozen development split) [E]. Second, OpenTimestamps Bitcoin Calendar proofs and League of Entropy drand beacons (6663734 and 6664089) created a hash-precommitted lookup store—proving cryptographically that the DNULLMM1 binary table and seed schedule existed before test evaluation, which is narrower than an externally peer-reviewed clinical statistical analysis plan [E].

Results Across All 6 Models and External Public Benchmarks

Evaluating Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, OpenAI gpt-oss-120b, xAI Grok 4.20, Alibaba Qwen 3.6 35B-A3B, and Google Gemma 4 E4B-it across 4,030 instances cleanly separates template memorization from genuine open-domain synthesis [E]:

  • Track-A Bounded Template Regime (N = 2,840, 10 cells): Single-turn models tied or trailed N1 on 9 of 10 bounded structured cells; only Opus 5.5 beat Shape D (+36.40 pp) on unindexed Tier-2 tau2_sqlite paraphrases. On unique_3sat_drat (N = 50), a 1,024-token output cap truncated Opus 5.5 at 5.2%, whereas raising thinking budget to 8,192 tokens reached 49/50 (98%), 6-turn O(m) clause-violation feedback reached 50/50 (100%), and classical CDCL+DRAT solver B1 solved 50/50 in < 1 ms with zero neural compute [E].
  • Track-B Unique External Public Benchmarks (N = 1,190): Where tasks require unseen code synthesis or novel schema composition, LLMs decisively beat Shape D: +60.00 pp on BFCL v3, +60.45 pp on tau-bench Retail, +95.00 pp on BigCodeBench v0.1.3, and +52.80 pp on SWE-bench Verified 12-way file localization (with exp-003 recording +45.83 pp for gpt-oss-120b and +44.17 pp for Grok 4.20) [E].
  • Upstream SWE-bench Verified Repositories (N = 6 real git trees): Cold Shape D patched 0/6 repositories; Claude Opus 5.5 passed full repository test suites on 5/6, Sonnet 5.5 on 4/6, and Grok 4.20 on 1/6 [E].

  • Track-A template saturation (K_eff = 6–12): A post-run audit documented in the primary paper showed that several Track-A bounded generators sampled from only 6 to 12 underlying structural templates, explaining why N1 saturated them easily [E].
  • Nearest-neighbor overfitting (N1 < N0 on tau-bench Retail): Greedy bigram matching (N1, 25.9%) actually underperformed strict abstaining lookup (N0, 39.6%) on tau-bench Retail by pasting superficially similar but semantically wrong tool arguments [E].
  • Exact recall vs. unseen generalization: Re-running the 6 SWE-bench repos at t = 2 after crystallizing verified t = 1 patches yields 5/6 hits at 0 LLM calls—demonstrating content-addressed memoization (exact recall), not transfer to new issues. Any commit that alters target AST digests or test contracts invalidates the cached entry (3.59x call and reported_j savings on BigCodeBench holds specifically under the tested Zipf(0.85) repeat distribution) [E, M].

Five-host SATB conformance and telemetry attribution audit (Thor INA238/INA3221 measured_j + 4 reported_j hosts; L0 wall analyzer unattached). Dedicated to the public domain under CC0-1.0.

Key Claims & Audited Scope ([T] / [E] / [M] / [S])

  1. [E · 5-Host Deterministic Replay] The sequential Rust SATB harness (ContextRule_v0 80% oldest-tool-output elision, Truncate_v0 8 + 8 KiB cap) passed 12/12 conformance checks (C1–C12) and replayed Shape D (15027705736) and C9 (149,747 B) with 0 byte diffs across macOS arm64, Tegra Linux aarch64, two x86-64 Linux hosts, and bare-metal Windows 11 Pro.
  2. [E · Falsifiers 2 & 3: Attribution Errors] Comparing ground-truth rail/counter deltas against cloud-native CPU-utilization proportional splitting (Kepler heuristic) revealed 32.59% to 89.88% energy attribution error (Falsifier 2), while Windows GetProcessTimes 15.625 ms scheduler-tick aliasing undercounted short subprocess bursts by -89.88% (Falsifier 3, resolved only via QueryProcessCycleTime + TerminateJobObject 2.458 ms cleanup).
  3. [E · Falsifier 6: Shared-Host Honesty] Whenever pre/post idle power drifted by > 5.0% due to co-tenant OS activity, Falsifier 6 automatically withheld net marginal attribution (A1 = null) while preserving raw unattributed measured_j / reported_j logs.

Methods, Baselines, Sample Sizes (N) & Licensing Scope

  • Hardware & Telemetry: (1) NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor (TI INA238 VIN L1 + 3-channel INA3221 VDD_GPU / VDD_CPU_SOC_MSS / VIN_SYS_5V0 L2 DC shunts, measured_j); (2) Apple M5 Max (IOReport L2 + ri_energy_nj L3 reported_j); (3) AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (0440 root:energy RAPL L2 + Radeon 8060S PPT reported_j); (4) Intel Core i9-13900H (RAPL psys L1 + pkg-0 L2 reported_j); (5) Windows 11 Pro (Core i7-1165G7 + RTX 2060 nvml.dll L2 reported_j). External AC wall analyzer (L0): not attached.
  • Workload & Suite: 12 harness conformance suites (C1–C12: truncation, context elision, timeout job-tree kill C10, canonical JSON/receipt replay C9) plus counterbalanced CPU, memory-bandwidth, and GPU-offload attribution stress workloads.
  • Baselines Compared: Kepler-style CPU-time-ratio energy attribution (Falsifier 2), Win32 GetProcessTimes tick accounting (Falsifier 3), and naive single-baseline idle subtraction (Falsifier 6).
  • Runs (N) & Uncertainty / Spread: 12/12 conformance pass across all 5 hosts (0 byte diffs); attribution error range 32.59%–89.88% across memory/GPU stress pairs; co-tenant drift threshold fixed at 5.0% pre/post quiescent shift.
  • Cold vs. Warm Caching Scope: Loopback proxy explicitly logs Shape D exact-replay hits separately from live Shape M/H/I model invocations so cached runs cannot masquerade as fresh inference.
  • Artifact & License Status: Envelope/non-mixing linter public in openIE-dev/openie-artifact-substrate (Apache-2.0); full multi-host raw telemetry CSVs published on research.openie.dev (CC0-1.0 text).

Problem, Telemetry Taxonomy (L0–L4 × A1–N) & Scope

Software energy papers routinely treat container CPU-share heuristics, OS process counters, and physical DC shunts as interchangeable "joules." SATB defines a two-dimensional provenance lattice crossing sensor boundary (L0 AC wall plug, L1 whole-board DC input, L2 SoC/package domain, L3 kernel per-process counter, L4 analytical proxy) with attribution discipline (A1 isolated quiesced net delta, A2 unisolated gross delta, D kernel-assigned, N withheld) [M, E].

Five-Host Audit Results & Exposed Attribution Failures

  • Physical shunt vs. proportional-CPU heuristics (Falsifier 2) [E]: On Jetson AGX Thor (INA238 + INA3221 measured_j) and dual-counter workstations (reported_j), memory-bound and GPU-dispatched tasks consumed minimal CPU ticks while drawing substantial DRAM/GPU rail power, causing Kepler-style CPU-utilization splitting to misattribute 32.59% to 89.88% of actual energy [E].
  • Windows scheduler-tick aliasing (Falsifier 3) [E]: On bare-metal Windows 11 Pro (Core i7-1165G7 + RTX 2060), GetProcessTimes quantizes execution to 15.625 ms (64 Hz) clock interrupts, undercounting short bursts by -89.88%; switching to hardware QueryProcessCycleTime plus TerminateJobObject (2.458 ms tree teardown in C10) closed the gap [E].
  • PLATYPUS-safe rootless Linux RAPL [E]: Following CVE-2020-8694 (PLATYPUS), Linux powercap files default to 0400 root:root; SATB documents dedicated 0440 root:energy group provisioning on dedicated test benches rather than sudo benchmark execution [E, S].

Limitations, Unmetered L0 Wall Boundary & Falsifier 6

  • No L0 AC wall-plug power analyzer: L0 (PSU losses + AC power factor, e.g., Yokogawa WT310E) was not attached on any of the five hosts (L0 = unmetered) [E].
  • Shared-host refusal (Falsifier 6): Whenever background OS tasks shifted pre/post idle baselines by > 5.0%, SATB refused to emit net A1 marginal joules—a conservative refusal that fired repeatedly on busy developer machines (e.g., 109/170 whole-chip windows in ai-reads-human) [E].

Key Claims & Audited Scope ([T] / [E] / [M] / [S])

  1. [T · Lean 4.36.0, 6/6 kernels] Horizon.lean and Paradox.lean machine-check 31 primary theorems (50 theorem/lemma declarations, 58,796 kernel declarations verified by con-leche and con-ron inside Linux bubblewrap with 0 sorry, 0 opaque, and 0 ofReduceBool) formalizing causal-cone exclusivity, fixed-point consistency, and salt-invalidated precomputation over abstract discrete models.
  2. [E/M · Deterministic Simulation, unmetered] Across N = 65,536 SHA-256 digests (32,768 FFT spectral bins in experiment F5 and M1–M8), 0 spectral bins crossed the Bonferroni-corrected significance threshold p = 10^-6, matching an unindexed white-noise null.
  3. [S · Literature Synthesis] Known closed-timelike-curve complexity classes (D-CTC = PSPACE, P-CTC = PP, Aaronson & Watrous 2009) collapse computationally bounded ciphers inside hypothetical fixed-point loops while leaving information-theoretic one-time pads intact; outside such loops, every real O(1) lookup is amortized Hellman precomputation (T * M^2 = N^2).

Methods, Baselines, Sample Sizes (N) & Licensing Scope

  • Hardware & Telemetry: Unmetered (joules = null, board_metered = false). Lean 4.36.0 lake check --paranoid executed inside Linux bubblewrap (bwrap); deterministic Python/Rust spectral scripts without hardware power probes.
  • Workload & Suite: 31 formal theorems (50 total Lean declarations), M1–M8 discrete horizon/tradeoff simulations, F5 SHA-256 FFT spectral scan (N = 65,536 digests), and a 195-entry anomaly/paradox literature catalog (TA001–TA081, AA01–AA40, P01–P74).
  • Baselines Compared: Uniform pseudorandom white-noise null (Bonferroni alpha = 10^-6 across 32,768 bins) for F5; unsalted vs. salted Hellman rainbow-table amortization curves for M1–M8.
  • Runs (N) & Uncertainty / Spread: Deterministic seeded SHA-256 counter sweep (N = 65,536 digests; exact reproducible max spectral peak within Gaussian/exponential null envelope; single seeded sweep, multi-seed variance not needed for deterministic hash check but limits sample horizon to 2^16).
  • Cold vs. Warm Caching Scope: Explicitly models offline precomputation ("warm rainbow table") vs. salted per-instance cold evaluation: adding an s-bit fresh salt multiplies precomputation table work by 2^s, forcing cold online work.
  • Artifact & License Status: Primary paper and 195-entry catalog (CC0-1.0); proof check logs and scripts self-checked by OpenIE (Apache-2.0 subset; not externally peer-reviewed).

Problem, Scope & Framing Qualifiers

This study asks a foundational boundary question: what separates sequential computation from spatial array indexing? Rather than claiming exotic physical effects, the paper proves and catalogs why "looking up tomorrow" is impossible in standard quantum and classical physics [S, T]. All CTC results (PSPACE / PP collapse of hardness assumptions) apply strictly to hypothetical Deutschian mathematical fixed-point models, not to realizable laboratory hardware [S, T].

Mechanism, Formal Proofs & Spectral Results

Three results anchor the paper:

  • Machine-checked horizon & salt theorems [T]: Across Horizon.lean and Paradox.lean (31 theorems verified across all 6/6 independent Lean checkers with 0 sorry), any state-indexed lookup table over an deterministic transition must pay at least linear offline state-visitation work prior to query arrival, and prepending a fresh unpredictable salt renders pre-built index tables statistically independent of the target.
  • Hellman precomputation tradeoff [S, M]: Hellman (1980) and Oechslin (2003) show that unsalted inversions trade online time T against precomputed memory M along T * M^2 = N^2 [S]. Simulated curves (M1–M8) illustrate how Bitcoin block-header chaining and TLS/Argon2 nonces reset the precomputation horizon to zero before each challenge exists [M].
  • Finite-sample SHA-256 spectral control [E]: Applying a 65,536-point discrete Fourier analysis across sequential SHA-256 outputs yields 0 / 32,768 frequency bins below p = 10^-6 [E].

Limitations, Negative Results & Falsifiers

  • Finite spectral power: Testing N = 65,536 (2^16) SHA-256 digests rules out gross linear periodicities at that sample size; it is not a cryptanalytic security proof against algebraic or differential attacks [M].
  • Abstract axiom boundary: Lean theorems verify discrete mathematical definitions of causal cones, fixed points, and finite maps; physical no-signalling and Gabor Delta t * Delta f >= 1/(4 pi) bounds rest on established physics literature [S], not proof-assistant axioms.
  • Catalog scope: The 195 cataloged timing/frequency anomalies (TA001–TA081, AA01–AA40, P01–P74) synthesize published metrology glitches (e.g., OPERA loose fiber connector), oscillator tolerances, and logical paradoxes from secondary and primary literature [S].

No hardware power meter or OS energy counter was used to support any claim in this study (energyClass = unmetered, joules = null, board_metered = false). Thermodynamic discussions inside the manuscript refer analytically to classical literature bounds rather than measured silicon energy.

  • Hellman (IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory, 1980) & Oechslin (CRYPTO 2003): Cryptanalytic time-memory tradeoffs (T * M^2 = N^2) and rainbow tables [S].

[E · Exact Definition of "98% Combined" (CTA-E5)] On the frozen 100-task, 5-regime deterministic-oracle benchmark (20 tasks/regime R1–R5), routed 10-paradigm synthesis DES-10 (GPT-OSS-120B + SAT/FD + causal do(X) + LUT6/FSM + Shape D behind deterministic gates) solved 98 / 100 (98.0%) tasks with 1 / 100 (1.0%) false commit and 1 / 100 abstention at 9.26x–26.87x higher Thor INA3221 measured_j coherence-per-joule—compared against <= 49 / 100 for every isolated paradigm C1–C10 (C9 3-agent NL debate 49/100 with 51% false commits; C1 solo LLM 48/100 with 52% false commits; C2 SAT/FD 30%; C8 LUT6/FSM 20%; C5 Shape D 16%; C4 MCTS 10%–11%; C7 do(X) 10%; C6/C10 4%; C3 unverified EBM 0%).
  3. [M/T · Explicit Analogical & Biomedical Scope Boundaries] (1) Mapping 24 biological signaling rungs (CL01–CL24, 3.8 Ga) to 38 AI milestones (AI01–AI38, 1950–2026) and agent models CA-M1..CA-M5 is an ex-post interpretive framing, strictly separate from falsifiable CTA-E1..E7 benchmarks; and (2) the 45 Lean 4.36.0 theorems (CTA-T1..T45, 0 sorry across 6/6 kernels in bwrap) verify an abstract mathematical state-machine model of opt-in consent (g_i(s_i, m) = 1)—NOT a clinical, biophysical, or hardware safety guarantee for human brains (as the paper itself documents: invasive human BCI readout BM07/BM08 is ~15–19 bit/s, BrainNet is ~0.02–0.5 bit/s, and 16/16 EV01–EV16 extracellular-vesicle CNS studies are preclinical animal/in-vitro models with 0 Phase III human trials).

  • Hardware & Telemetry: (1) measured_j (board_metered = true): NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor (TI INA3221 ch2 VDD_CPU_SOC_MSS L2 + INA238 VIN L1 @ 500 Hz ABBA windows) for CTA-E4 and CTA-E5; (2) reported_j (board_metered = false): Intel Core i9-13900H (RAPL pkg/core), Apple M3 Ultra & Apple M5 Max (Darwin L3 ri_energy_nj), and AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (RAPL core/pkg) for CTA-E1..E4.
  • Workload & Suite: CTA-E1/E4: 50,000 iterations of 1 KiB WAI1 (BLAKE3 + Ed25519) envelope sign/verify vs. JSON/prose multi-agent handoffs; CTA-E2: 60-task multi-hop pipeline (59/60 verified close, 0/60 silent drift); CTA-E5: 100-task, 5-regime (20 tasks × R1 arithmetic/logic, R2 causal do(X), R3 FSM/parity, R4 exact retrieval, R5 code/spec synthesis) 10-camp evaluation; 45 Lean 4.36.0 theorems (QuorumRatchet, OrchestrationFlow, EnzymaticSynthesis); CA-M1..CA-M5 stylized biological simulations.
  • Baselines Compared: Multi-agent natural-language prose relays (AutoGen/ChatDev-style debate C9: 49/100 accuracy, 51/100 false commits, 69.89 J/handoff on Thor) and solo GPT-OSS-120B (C1: 48/100, 52/100 false commits) vs. binary WAI1 envelopes + routed DES-10 (98/100 accuracy, 1/100 false commit).
  • Runs (N) & Uncertainty / Spread: CTA-E4: N = 50,000 iterations per host (p50 latencies: 50.13 us Thor, 23.84 us Core i9, 29.54 us M3 Ultra, 33.12 us Ryzen AI Max+ 395). CTA-E2: N = 60 tasks (59/60, Wilson 95% CI 91.1%–99.7%). CTA-E5: N = 100 tasks (98/100 DES-10, 1/100 false commit). CA-M1..M5: seeded agent-based simulations ([M]).
  • Cold vs. Warm Caching Scope: CTA-E2 and CTA-E5 evaluate cold (F_NOCACHE) task instances first (59/60 and 98/100); post-gate crystallization (Proposition 1 stationary horizon) is accounted separately so memoized hits never inflate cold multi-paradigm accuracy.

Host-Separated Handoff Telemetry (CTA-E4) & DES-10 (CTA-E5)

Presenting the per-host table from CTA-E4 (1 KiB BLAKE3 + Ed25519 verification over N = 50,000 iterations) removes any cross-machine confusion between Jetson Thor shunt energy and desktop clock speed [E]:

  • Host & Architecture: NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor (aarch64 Tegra) — Telemetry Tier (board_metered): measured_j: TI INA3221 VDD_CPU_SOC_MSS (true) — p50 Verify Latency: 50.13 us — Energy per 1 KiB Verify: 927.30 uJ (3.89 mJ VIN) — Scope Note: Whole CPU/SoC/MSS rail (~18.5 W); 75,374x < NL prose relay
  • Host & Architecture: Intel Core i9-13900H (x86-64 Linux) — Telemetry Tier (board_metered): reported_j: RAPL pkg / core (false) — p50 Verify Latency: 23.84 us (25.95–27.04 us E1) — Energy per 1 KiB Verify: 642.38 uJ pkg (550.59 uJ core) — Scope Note: Faster out-of-order x86 clock, modeled counter
  • Host & Architecture: Apple M3 Ultra (arm64 macOS) — Telemetry Tier (board_metered): reported_j: Darwin L3 ri_energy_nj (false) — p50 Verify Latency: 29.54 us — Energy per 1 KiB Verify: 90.81 uJ (L3 process) — Scope Note: Excludes unattributed DRAM/system rails
  • Host & Architecture: AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (Zen 5 Linux) — Telemetry Tier (board_metered): reported_j: RAPL core (false) — p50 Verify Latency: 33.12 us — Energy per 1 KiB Verify: 201.27 uJ core — Scope Note: Modeled per-core counter

In CTA-E5 (100 frozen tasks across 5 regimes × 20 tasks), every single-paradigm camp failed outside its native regime (C1 solo GPT-OSS-120B 48/100 with 52% false commits; C9 3-agent prose debate 49/100 with 51% false commits; symbolic C2 30/100; causal C7 10/100), whereas routing each subproblem through typed binary envelopes and deterministic checkers (DES-10) closed 98 / 100 (98.0%) with 1 / 100 (1.0%) false commit [E].

Framing Qualifiers: Evolutionary Rungs & Formal Consent Theorems

  • Biological ratchet (CL01–CL24) & stylized models (CA-M1..CA-M5) [M, S]: Agent simulations CA-M1..CA-M5 (95.49%–99.17% thresholded quorum signaling savings vs. continuous broadcast; Physarum tube pruning; Boids k = 7 topological cohesion) are low-dimensional mathematical illustrations of published biology models—they motivate thresholded event-driven orchestration (Rung 4–6), not cross-kingdom equivalence proofs [M, S].
  • Why 45 Lean theorems (CTA-T1..T45) do NOT certify BCI safety [T, S]: In OrchestrationFlow.lean, opt-in consent is modeled as a pure predicate g_i(s_i, m) = 1 on abstract state transitions [T]. Real neural tissue interfaces face physical electrode degradation, non-stationary spike decoding (~15–19 bit/s in human intracortical trials BM07/BM08, Willett et al. Nature 2021/2023), and 0 Phase III human CNS extracellular-vesicle trials (EV01–EV16)—domains governed by biomedical engineering and clinical ethics, never by discrete typecheckers [S].

Limitations, 1% Gate Escape & Partial Code Availability

  • Gates reduce but do not remove false commits (1/100 in DES-10): Even on CTA-E5, DES-10 admitted 1 false commit (1.0%) and abstained on 1 task (1.0%), demonstrating empirically that an imperfect oracle check can still pass an incorrect edge-case candidate [E].
  • Benchmark stratification bias: CTA-E5 weights five distinct computational regimes equally (20% each); on pure open-ended natural-language chat (Z3), symbolic/causal/LUT6 specialists contribute 0% and DES-10 reduces to C1 [M].

item.content:encoded:
Separates Jetson AGX Thor TI INA3221/INA238 physical DC shunts (measured_j) from workstation chip counters (reported_j), Cortex-M55 DWT cycles, and FPGA VCD est_j, tying 91.67% (44/48) and 62.50% (10/16) to exact model/gate arms.

Signed Provenance · Self-Checked (human_in_gate = false; automated build, benchmark, and proof-checking scripts ran without manual override — not externally peer-reviewed; see Verification & AI-Use Disclosure and Epistemic Glossary).

Canonical Post-Review Essay (rel="canonical"): https://blog.openie.dev/posts/lut-adapt/

Primary Research Paper: https://research.openie.dev/papers/lut-adapt/

1-Command Replication Kit: https://github.com/openIE-dev/openie-research-experiments/tree/main/replicate · Study Repository: https://github.com/openIE-dev/lut-adapt-ai

Canonical Artifact ID: blake3:tv:f5f2551c2e873bdc7af0ce1e380b0a888679c3ade804cbec637a62785734ec8d · Evidence Tags: [T] · [E] · [M] · [S] · Telemetry Class: measured_j

Stratified lut-adapt-ai (dc45357) results: Jetson AGX Thor DC shunt (measured_j), 4-vendor CubeCL GPU & coding cascades (reported_j), and FPGA VCD (est_j). Dedicated to the public domain under CC0-1.0.

Key Claims & Audited Scope ([T] / [E] / [M] / [S])

  1. [E · Resolved Telemetry Contradiction (measured_j vs. reported_j vs. est_j)] Earlier summaries mixed board_metered = true with workstation counter prose. Grounded in src/content/papers/lut-adapt.md, measured_j (board_metered = true) applies strictly to NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor physical TI INA3221 (VDD_CPU_SOC_MSS L2) and INA238 (VIN L1) DC current shunts (Claims LA-24, LA-28, LA-32, LA-33, LA-38); workstation LLM and 4-vendor CubeCL GPU runs (Apple M5 Max, AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395, Intel Core i9-13900H, RTX 4050/2060) use on-chip reported_j (board_metered = false); live Alif Ensemble E3 (OpenMV-AE3 Cortex-M55 @ 400 MHz) reports hardware DWT cycles (board_metered = false); and FPGA gateware power (Kria KV260 15.59 est_mW, Artix-7 XC7A200T 0.86 est_W) is Verilator VCD + datasheet est_j (measured_j = null).
  2. [E · Named Configurations Behind 91.67% (44/48) and 62.50% (10/16)] On the 48-task (16 specs × 3 waves) coding bakeoff (Claim LA-17), 91.67% (44/48, 0 broken commits admitted) was achieved by MoL + Rung 3d Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B with bounded 1,536–2,200 <think> tokens and deterministic unittest gate (vs. 87.50% Arm G without <think> and 77.08% standalone Qwen3.6-35B-A3B). On the 16-task (8 specs × 2 waves) hard adversarial coding suite (Claim LA-21), 62.50% (10/16) was achieved by the MoL Apex cascade (BenesLUT6 + .mol/ + counterexample escalation across Devstral-Small-2-24B-Instruct and nvidia/Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B) (vs. 43.75% standalone 120B-A12B and 31.25% standalone 24B).
  3. [E/T · 80 Six-Input (6-Bit, 64-Entry) LUT6 Truth Tables & 58 Lean Proofs] Rung 0 routes inputs through a 512 × 512 Beneš/Waksman permutation network into 80 six-input (6-bit, 64-entry) LUT6 truth tables (and 4 KB CompactLut6Page + 672 B antisymmetric 40-entry zero-MUL T-MAC tail), achieving 162.56–162.71 nJ/op (87.00x–87.25x CpJ vs. 14,143.46 nJ/op INT8 Micro-MLP) on Thor INA3221 measured_j, alongside 58 six-kernel-verified Lean 4.36.0 theorems and mechanical Charon + Aeneas #![no_std] Rust-to-Lean extraction (6 core functions).

Methods, Baselines, Sample Sizes (N) & Licensing Scope

  • Hardware & Telemetry: (1) measured_j: NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor (TI INA3221 ch2 VDD_CPU_SOC_MSS + INA238 VIN @ 500 Hz 2 ms trapezoidal ABBA integration, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=""); (2) reported_j: Apple M5 Max 128 GB (IOReport/ri_energy_nj), AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 + Radeon 8060S (RAPL + PPT), Intel Core i9-13900H (RAPL), NVIDIA RTX 4050 / RTX 2060 (NVML); (3) MCU cycles: live USB OpenMV-AE3 (Alif E3 Cortex-M55 @ 400 MHz DWT); (4) est_j: Verilator 5.054 VCD + AMD DS925/DS181 on XCK26 & XC7A200T.
  • Workload & Suite: LA-17 (48 coding tasks = 16 specs × 3 waves), LA-21 (16 hard adversarial coding tasks = 8 specs × 2 waves), 32-task BigCodeBench v0.1.3 slice (29/32 = 90.62%), LA-24 6-host downward-compilation matrix (W1–W5), LA-25 4-vendor Burn 0.22.1 / CubeCL GPU shader suite, LA-36 64-query bimodal wearable stream (48 daily + 16 PhD), and LA-37 32 open SuperGPQA hard + MathArena AIME/HMMT 2025 calibration items.
  • Baselines Compared: Standalone Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (77.08%), Devstral-Small-2-24B (31.25%), Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B (43.75%), INT8/BF16 Micro-MLP (64->32->16), LittleBit-2 MAC, dense 256-expert MoE, and UW/Meta Sensente/uLM-28M (28.84M collaborative prefix masking).
  • Runs (N) & Uncertainty / Spread: Thor measured_j (LA-24): 4/4 counterbalanced ABBA pairs (< 0.06% VDD_GPU drift, 0.19% VIN drift). Coding suites: N = 48 (44/48), N = 16 (10/16), N = 32 BigCodeBench (29/32), N = 64 wearable queries, N = 32 SuperGPQA/AIME/HMMT items (greedy/seeded deterministic evaluation; multi-seed LLM temperature variance not recorded).
  • Cold vs. Warm Caching Scope: Explicitly separated: Wave 1 in LA-17/LA-21 runs cold (escalating to 35B or 24B/120B behind the unittest gate), whereas Wave 2/3 hit crystallized .mol/ / LUT6 entries (Delta T* = 0.1084 < 1 episode break-even on Thor when a compiled skill is reused, vs. net compile overhead if N_reuse = 0; hle:3r2s canary guard blocks benchmark crystallization).
  • Artifact & License Status: Apache-2.0 public repository at https://github.com/openIE-dev/lut-adapt-ai (commit dc45357) and openIE-dev/openie-research-experiments; self-checked by OpenIE, open for independent replication.

Strict Telemetry Stratification (Thor measured_j vs. Workstation reported_j vs. FPGA est_j)

lut-adapt spans six CPU/GPU hosts, two bare-metal MCUs, and two FPGA targets. Keeping its four evidence tiers orthogonal (measured_j ⊥ reported_j ⊥ cycles ⊥ est_j) resolves the earlier summary’s "no board shunt" vs. board_metered = true contradiction [E]:

  • Physical DC Shunt (measured_j, board_metered = true): Recorded exclusively on NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor via hwmon5 TI INA3221 (VDD_CPU_SOC_MSS isolated CPU/SoC rail) and hwmon6 TI INA238 (VIN whole-board rail) at 500 Hz across ABBA windows: W2 Sub1Bit-LUT6 saves 3.74x CPU J (7.76 vs. 28.98 J), W3 Expert-AirMoL saves 34.21x (0.98 vs. 33.36 J), lut6-core vertical bit-slicing reaches 162.56–162.71 nJ/op (87.00x–87.25x CpJ vs. 14,143.46 nJ/op INT8 Micro-MLP), Antisym-40 zero-MUL T-MAC reaches 8,594.93 nJ/op (1.65x CpJ), and the 56-bit 4-token wearable epistemic gate uses 2,803.25 nJ vs. 623,920.52 nJ (222.57x) for 1/16th of a uLM-28M layer [E].
  • On-Chip Counters (reported_j, board_metered = false): Used for all workstation LLM cascades (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B, Oct–Nov 2026 looped Inkling-2-Mini 4.29x and Dory1.0-4B 3.86x LUT6 speculative burst cuts on M5 Max L3) and 4-vendor single-source Rust CubeCL GPU shaders (Apple Metal, AMD Radeon 8060S Vulkan, NVIDIA RTX 4050 Vulkan, Intel Iris Xe Vulkan, max FP32 err <= 1.79 × 10^-7) [E].
  • MCU DWT Cycles & FPGA est_j (board_metered = false): Live USB-attached OpenMV-AE3 (Alif E3 Cortex-M55 @ 400 MHz) records cycle counts (173.83x scalar LUT6, 11.17x T-MAC vs. INT8 MLP), while Kria KV260 (15.59 est_mW) and Artix-7 XC7A200T (0.86 est_W) are Verilator VCD + datasheet est_j [E].

Coding & Epistemic Cascade Results (Cold Wave 1 vs. Warm Wave 2/3)

  • 91.67% (44/48, Claim LA-17): Pairing MoL with Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (1,536–2,200 <think> tokens + unittest gate) solved 44/48 tasks across 3 waves (vs. 87.50% without <think> and 77.08% standalone 35B). Wave 1 pays cold 35B generation; Waves 2–3 amortize verified .mol/ skills [E].
  • 62.50% (10/16, Claim LA-21): On 16 hard adversarial coding tasks (8 specs × 2 waves), escalating across BenesLUT6 -> .mol/ -> Devstral-Small-2-24B -> Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B (58.1 GB RSS) solved 10/16 (62.50%) vs. 7/16 (43.75%) standalone 120B and 5/16 (31.25%) standalone 24B—candidly leaving 6/16 (37.5%) unsolved [E].
  • Wearable SRAM fit & frontier calibration (LA-36, LA-37): Wearable-MoL fits Rung 0 in 5,984 B (9.13% of 64 KB watch SRAM) vs. 13.75 MB (214x overflow) for Sensente/uLM-28M, suppresses 15/16 (93.75% -> 0 observed) wrong spoken prefixes on whiteboard PhD queries via EpistemicHold, and on 32 open SuperGPQA hard + AIME/HMMT 2025 items cuts RMS calibration error 5.37x (70.62% -> 13.14%) while scoring 0/16 (0%, abstaining) on Exact-Match Olympiad items where 24B/35B models also scored 0/16 [E].

Limitations & Open Boundaries

  • Cold novel tasks still require large neural models: 80-LUT6 / 4 KB CompactLut6Page crystals compress recurring bounded skills (H <= 1.25 bits in the 4-part Means Test); high-entropy open prose and unseen AIME/HMMT Olympiad proofs (0/16 solved) are refused to higher rungs or abstained [E].
  • Gated cais/hle respected without bypass: cais/hle returned HTTP 403 in automated runs and was not bypassed; LA-37 evaluated 32 open SuperGPQA hard + MathArena 2025 items under the HLE calibration protocol instead [E].
  • Unprobed M.2 FPGA rails: Numato Aller A7 (XC7A200T, openXC7 320.62 MHz .bit) awaits inline +3.3 V / +5 V Kelvin shunts to promote 0.86 est_W to measured_j (LA-F30) [E].

Energy & Telemetry Scope

Every comparison stays strictly inside its own telemetry class: Thor INA3221/INA238 (measured_j), per-host RAPL/IOReport/NVML (reported_j), Cortex-M55 DWT cycles, and Verilator VCD (est_j).

Analytical separation between single-task specification satiation and fleet-wide Jevons rebound (joules = null, unmetered). Dedicated to the public domain under CC0-1.0.

Key Claims & Audited Scope ([T] / [E] / [M] / [S])

  1. [M · Micro-Level Task Satiation] On any task governed by a sound binary completeness check C(z) = 1 (such as an exact compile+test repair or proved theorem), marginal utility of extra tokens after the first verified hit is zero—contrasting with open-ended creative or adversarial loops that lack a stopping criterion.
  2. [M/S · Macro-Level Rebound Caveat] Micro-efficiency does not guarantee lower grid electricity: under the standard elasticity identity d ln E_total / d ln eta = epsilon_d - 1, cutting joules per task expands the set of economically viable automated workflows and raises total fleet power whenever demand price elasticity epsilon_d > 1 (backfire / Jevons paradox).
  3. [S · Empirical Macro Context] Synthesizes Nordhaus (1996) lighting lumen-price history (> 1,000x efficiency gain paired with rising total lighting electricity share) and IEA (2024/2026) global datacenter electricity projections (~415 TWh toward ~945 TWh by 2030).

Methods, Baselines, Sample Sizes (N) & Licensing Scope

  • Hardware & Telemetry: Unmetered (joules = null, board_metered = false). Analytical microeconomic stopping-time models paired with published macro-energy elasticity literature.
  • Workload & Suite: No primary hardware benchmark run in this study; synthesizes historical efficiency/rebound series and IEA datacenter electricity reports.
  • Baselines Compared: Closed-specification gated tasks (C(z) in {0,1} finite stopping rule) vs. unbounded best-of-N / open-ended quality tournaments.
  • Runs (N) & Uncertainty / Spread: Not applicable (N = 0 primary lab trials; cites published IEA scenario ranges and Sorrell 2009 econometric elasticity intervals).
  • Cold vs. Warm Caching Scope: Notes that exact-match caching lowers marginal cost on recurring queries toward zero, further steepening the micro price drop that drives new extensive-margin adoption.
  • Artifact & License Status: Public-domain manuscript (CC0-1.0) at research.openie.dev/papers/satiation/; self-checked, not externally peer-reviewed.

Problem: Why Micro-Efficiency Claims Overshoot Macro Grid Reality

Engineering blogs routinely extrapolate a 10x or 100x kernel energy reduction into an equivalent cut in global datacenter power. satiation was written specifically to reject that naive extrapolation [M, S]. By separating the intensive margin (joules spent to close one fixed task) from the extensive margin (how many tasks society chooses to run once each task costs millicents instead of dollars), the paper reconciles bounded per-task verification with rising aggregate AI power draw [M, S].

Two Regimes: Bounded UnitSpecs vs. Elastic Extensive Margins

  • Bounded per-task satiation [M]: When a caller needs a specific file parsed, a deterministic state step run, or a bug patched against a sound specification, stopping immediately upon C(z) = 1 removes wasted post-solution sampling (such as 30x same-task agent token variance documented by Bai, Huang & Wang 2026) [M, S].
  • Extensive-margin Jevons rebound [S, M]: Jevons (1865), Khazzoom (1980), Brookes (1990), Saunders (1992), and Nordhaus (1996) demonstrate that drastic reductions in the cost of an intermediate input (coal per horsepower-hour, watts per lumen, or joules per verified inference) induce substitution and new application categories [S]. Even if every individual coding check drops 100x in energy, running continuous background verification across millions of repositories can increase aggregate kWh [M].

Limitations & Unresolved Elasticity Parameters

  • Demand elasticity for AI tasks is unmeasured: Whether long-run price elasticity epsilon_d for verified software/automation tasks sits below 1 (partial rebound, net energy savings) or above 1 (Jevons backfire) is an open empirical macro-econometric question not measured here [M, S].
  • Positional / adversarial arms races do not satiate: Tasks with relative payoffs (high-frequency trading, ad-auction bidding, cyber offense/defense) lack a finite C(z) = 1 satiation point regardless of gate design [M].

This study is unmetered (joules = null, board_metered = false); datacenter terawatt-hour figures (~415 TWh to ~945 TWh) are cited directly from International Energy Agency (IEA) reports [S].

Key Claims & Audited Scope ([T] / [E] / [M] / [S])

  1. [E · Reconciled 49.04 mJ vs. 15.44 J vs. 2,221 Checks (reported_j)] Earlier summaries conflated three separate workloads from rce-facts.json: 49.04 mJ (7.32 ms, Apple M5 Max L3 reported_j) is the cost of one single-Form rce check invocation; 15.44 J (2.32 s, ~249 mJ/Form) is the cost of checking, running, and multi-target emitting all 62 valid example Forms (60 top-level + 2 package Forms, alongside 13 syntax-reject and 73 type/admissibility-reject tests); and 2,221 / 2,236 (0 failures, 15 unsupported/reserved) is the normative conformance test count across 311 spec clauses (not 2,221 × 49 mJ). Moreover, rce CLI receipts themselves currently emit deterministic integer C.6 fuel units rather than reading OS host.Energy counters natively (§1, §6.3).
  2. [T · Honest Lean 4.36.0 Proof Boundary] Across 97 completed .lean files in spec/lean/ (f87d6af2), 0 sorry, 0 opaque, and 0 ofReduceBool appear across 1,264 source theorem/lemma declarations (5,393 kernel theorem constants verified by all 6/6 independent checkers in bwrap at 22,354.77 J Linux RAPL reported_j)—alongside 12 unproved Draft-0.9 theorem statements in Appendix F.9 (T42–T56 except T48, T51, T53), plus T60 and parts of T57, T59, T61, while Appendix C concurrency theorems (T16–T31) are proved on abstract models rather than the Rust evaluator.
  3. [T/E · Scoped Totality Guarantee] Rather than claiming RCE "removes undefined crashes," its totality discipline prevents stuck or non-terminating step evaluations within the modeled total Form core (requiring every event either to step or record a state-preserving kept step T8), excluding host OS failures, FFI boundaries, target-language compiler bugs, hardware faults, and open input-entry item #15.

Methods, Baselines, Sample Sizes (N) & Licensing Scope

  • Hardware & Telemetry: Apple M5 Max (128 GB, macOS 27.2.1, Darwin L3 ri_energy_nj reported_j) for 49.04 mJ single-Form check and 15.44 J 62-Form suite; x86-64 Linux RAPL package-0 (22,354.77 J, 319.80 s reported_j) for 6-kernel lake check --paranoid. measured_j = null (board_metered = false).
  • Workload & Suite: 62 valid Form blueprints (60 top-level + 2 package), 13 syntax-reject and 73 type/admissibility-reject negative tests, 2,236 normative conformance checks (311 clauses), 837 Rust unit tests (159 files), 77 canonical JSON vectors, and 97 Lean 4.36.0 proof files.
  • Baselines Compared: Byte-for-byte trace parity across 4 reference emitters (Rust, Python, JavaScript, Scala; plus CLI verilog/wasm targets); literature context from DéjàVu GitHub clone density (70%, Lopes et al. 2017) and TBar Defects4J repair protocols (§7–§8, planned empirically in rce-jepa).
  • Runs (N) & Uncertainty / Spread: Conformance & Lean checks are deterministic (2,221/2,236 pass, 0 fail; 6/6 Lean kernels pass). Apple M5 Max 49.04 mJ (7.32 ms) and 15.44 J (2.32 s): aggregate suite means recorded on 2026-11-22 in rce-facts.json (Spread: per-run SD/IQR not recorded in single-pass receipt summary).
  • Cold vs. Warm Caching Scope: Language specification separates cold candidate search (G1–G3) from G0 content-addressed shape lookup keyed by nameless structural Form hash (T7); rce paper itself measures checker/language invariants while rce-jepa benchmarks G0–G2 repair streams.
  • Artifact & License Status: Apache-2.0 public repository at https://github.com/openIE-dev/rce (commit f87d6af2) + browser playground (openie-dev.github.io/rce); self-checked by OpenIE, open for independent replication.

Reconciling Workload Scopes (49.04 mJ, 15.44 J, and 2,221 Checks)

Inspecting src/data/rce-facts.json and §1 / §6.3 of src/content/papers/rce.md separates three numbers that short video/blog summaries previously compressed together [E]:

  1. 49.04 mJ (7.32 ms on Apple M5 Max L3 ri_energy_nj, reported_j): External OS counter cost of one single-Form rce check run.
  1. 15.44 J (2.32 s on Apple M5 Max L3 reported_j): External OS counter cost of running the complete 62-Form example suite (syntax/type/totality checking plus multi-target Rust, Python, JS, and Scala trace verification across 60 standalone and 2 package Forms, ~249 mJ/Form end-to-end).
  1. 2,221 / 2,236 Conformance Checks (0 failures, 15 unsupported/reserved Draft-0.9 clauses): Normative clause assertions across 311 specification rules (104 core grammar rules / 1,028 LR states with 0 shift/reduce conflicts). Furthermore, §1 candidly discloses that openIE-dev/rce main does not yet implement rce host calibrate or native host.Energy OS-counter receipts inside the checker binary; internal receipts record deterministic integer C.6 fuel units [E].

Theorem Audit (5,393 Constants vs. 12 Unproved Draft-0.9 Statements)

Scientific precision requires reporting both proved and unproved parts of Draft 0.9 [T]:

  • Completed Lean 4.36.0 proofs (f87d6af2): 97 .lean files containing 1,264 hand-written theorem/lemma declarations elaborate to 5,393 kernel theorem constants (5,537 under Lean 4.12.0 due to elaborator splitter differences) with 0 sorry, 0 custom axioms, 0 opaque, and 0 Lean.ofReduceBool, accepted by all 6/6 independent checkers (con-leche, con-ron, lean4lean, nanoda, leanchecker --paranoid, and Lean v4.36.0) inside a networkless bubblewrap sandbox [T].
  • Unproved Draft-0.9 statements & model gaps: Appendix F.9 states theorems T42–T56, of which T48, T51, and T53 are proved over models while 12 Draft-0.9 theorems remain unproved; T60 and full-alphabet/evaluator extensions of T57, T59, T61, and T62 remain open in spec/book/10-theorems.md; and concurrency theorems T16–T31 apply to abstract core models rather than mechanical extraction of the Rust reference checker [T, E].

Limitations: Identifiers, Comprehension, and Totality Boundaries

  • Modeled core totality vs. real-world host faults: Theorem T8 guarantees every transition within a valid Form terminates in a new state or a logged kept step—preventing stuck evaluations inside the modeled language core, not OS OOM kills, FFI wrapper bugs, target-compiler miscompilations, or cosmic-ray bit flips (and entry-contract check #15 in §10 remains open) [T, E].
  • Nameless hashing vs. LLM/human readability (§2.1): While positional hashing (T7) canonicalizes variable names out of the Form digest, §2.1 cites empirical software-comprehension studies ([139]) showing frontier LLMs lose 11–29 points of summarization/prediction accuracy when identifiers are stripped—meaning human/model side-tables carrying identifier concepts remain essential [S].

Signed Provenance · Self-Checked (human_in_gate = false; automated build, benchmark, and proof-checking scripts ran without manual override — not externally peer-reviewed; see Verification & AI-Use Disclosure and Epistemic Glossary).

Canonical Post-Review Essay (rel="canonical"): https://blog.openie.dev/posts/rce-jepa/

Canonical Artifact ID: blake3:tv:019888e27dfd3fb4b49ea3e29a210c3c3de5f4565c4d71c3b42ed1e7f5114b8e · Evidence Tags: [E] · [M] · [S] · Telemetry Class: reported_j

Measured 3-Gear repair cascade (111/151 deterministic + FormJEPA-v1 + FormEBM-v3 + H15-Iterative), including FormJEPA-v1 H5/H11 negatives and 0.5278 cross-module OOD boundary (reported_j). Dedicated to the public domain under CC0-1.0.

Key Claims & Audited Scope ([T] / [E] / [M] / [S])

  1. [E · 3-Gear Cold Repair Cascade (reported_j)] On 151 real git-history and defect tasks (openIE-dev/rce@1762fb4b), deterministic rungs a..e solved 111/151 (73.5%, 0 model calls). On the 40 open residual tasks (H15), FormJEPA-v1 (8.42M trainable params trained on 1,106 strictly disjoint Form shapes; 58.65 mJ at k = 1, 474.76 mJ at k = 16 Zen 5 RAPL core reported_j) solved 22/40 (k = 1) and 27/40 (k = 16), matching local Qwen 3.6 35B-A3B (27/40 at 84.25 J/cand), while bounded <= 5-turn checker feedback + public stdlib/lib signature headers (H15-Iterative) closed 40/40 (100%, 0 contradictions) on Claude Opus 5.5 (USD 1.81) and Sonnet 5.5 (USD 1.11), and 39/40 on Grok 4.20 Reasoning.
  2. [E · Candid Latent-Energy Negatives & Progression] Uncalibrated FormJEPA-v1 L2 latent distance reached only 0.618 AUROC on H5 (inconclusive, < 0.85 target) and 36.0% strict 5-step monotonicity on H11. Contrastive FormEBM-v2 (5.85M) lifted unseen-shape H5 to 0.8922 and H11 to 93.0% (rho = 0.9931) but inverted to 0.2585 zero-shot cross-task AUROC on large multi-line H15 migrations; span-normalized two-head FormEBM-v3 (6.05M) reached 0.9437 H5 AUROC, 94.0%/92.0% H11 monotonicity, and resolved the OOD inversion to 0.5278 (0.6018 on >= 10-token rewrites)—still plateauing near 0.53 across unseen multi-module cryptographic APIs (mls, pq, pqxdh) without cross-file signatures.
  3. [E · Cold vs. Zipf(0.85) Replay & Rung-f Refusal] Crystallizing verified repairs into DNULLMM1 (0.325 us, 1.77 uJ M5 Max L3 reported_j) replays 40/40 exact tasks at 0 calls and cuts Gear-2 frontier episodes 16.67x (200 -> 12 episodes) on a 200-arrival Zipf(0.85) stream—strictly via verified memoization, not unseen generalization. Meanwhile, rce repair criterion (3/119 = 2.5% > 2.0% threshold) returned holds: false, keeping external-proposal rung f in observe mode rather than promoting it prematurely.

Methods, Baselines, Sample Sizes (N) & Licensing Scope

  • Hardware & Telemetry: Apple M5 Max (128 GB, Darwin L3 ri_energy_nj reported_j: 49.04 mJ rce check, 1.771 uJ DNULLMM1 mmap probe) and AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 / Radeon 8060S (Linux powercap RAPL core reported_j: 58.65–474.76 mJ FormJEPA-v1, 47.09 mJ FormEBM-v2, 232.45 mJ FormEBM-v3; net package reported_j withheld as None under Falsifier 6 at 13.7%–37.7% co-tenant drift). measured_j = null.
  • Workload & Suite: Disjoint 1,387-Form corpus (1,106 train, 144 val, 137 unseen test shapes; 0 overlap with eval benchmarks via 4-layer nameless hash exclusion), 200 unseen H5 candidate beams (3,064 candidates), 100 unseen 5-step H11 corruption chains, 151-task rce repair git-history ladder, and 40 open residual tasks (H15).
  • Baselines Compared: Deterministic rce repair rungs a..e (111/151), unreranked & Siamese-L2 beam selection (22.5% / 25.0% top-1 vs. 83.44% FormEBM-v3), local Qwen 3.6 35B-A3B (27/40), and cloud Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, and Grok 4.20 (single-shot 34/40 vs. <= 5-turn 40/40).
  • Runs (N) & Uncertainty / Spread: N = 200 unseen H5 beams (3,064 candidates), N = 100 H11 chains (median Spearman rho = 1.0000, IQR shaded in Fig. 10), N = 50 unconstrained random walks (38.0% strict step inequality), N = 151 ladder tasks, N = 40 H15 residual tasks, N = 40,000 mmap probes, M = 200 Zipf(0.85) arrivals.
  • Cold vs. Warm Caching Scope: Strict 4-layer nameless-digest deduplication between training (1,106 shapes) and cold evaluation (137 unseen shapes, 151 ladder, 40 H15). Warm DNULLMM1 (40/40 exact recall, 7/9 alpha-renamed hits via rce fmt nameless) and Zipf(0.85) (16.67x fewer Gear-2 episodes) are reported separately from cold first-exposure accuracy.
  • Artifact & License Status: Checker/ladder public at https://github.com/openIE-dev/rce (Apache-2.0); preregistered SHA-256 manifests (B30–B36) and interactive data at research.openie.dev/living/rce-jepa/ (CC0-1.0); self-checked, not externally peer-reviewed.

How Form-Space JEPA / EBM Differs from Pixel/Video JEPA

LeCun (2022) and Assran et al. (I-JEPA 2023, V-JEPA 2 2025) introduced Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures to predict abstract target representations without pixel-level reconstruction [S]. RCE-JEPA tests that architecture on discrete, quotient-normalized RCE Form ASTs paired with an exact external oracle (rce check + W-MUT-1 mutation adequacy + rce equiv) [E]. Unlike continuous vision tasks, a single unbound identifier invalidates an entire program—which is why FormJEPA-v1 needed a latent-conditioned typed edit decoder and why uncalibrated Smooth-L1 latent distance (0.618 AUROC) failed H5 until replaced by contrastive/span-normalized FormEBM-v2/v3 [E].

Cold Repair Results vs. Warm Zipf(0.85) Crystallization

  • Cold first-exposure hierarchy [E]: Deterministic solver rungs a..e close 111/151 (73.5%) with zero neural weights. On the 40 remaining real git-history defects, FormJEPA-v1 (8.42M params) closes 27/40 (67.5% at k = 16, 0.475 J Zen 5 core reported_j), matching 35B local Qwen 3.6 (27/40, 84.25 J/cand) on syntax/capability repairs while scoring 0/9 on multi-module cryptographic stdlib migrations (hpke, mls, pq, pqxdh) [E]. Supplying stripped stdlib/lib public headers and <= 5 turns of verbatim checker diagnostics (H15-Iterative) closes 40/40 on Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 with 0 semantic contradictions [E].
  • Warm DNULLMM1 replay & invalidation scope [E]: Storing those 40 verified repairs in DNULLMM1 replays 40/40 exact repeats in 0.325 us (1.77 uJ M5 Max L3 reported_j) and 7/9 alpha-renamed variants via rce fmt nameless, cutting frontier episodes 16.67x (200 -> 12) on a 200-request Zipf(0.85) stream—while any change to imported stdlib signatures or spec invariants invalidates the stored entry and re-triggers cold checking [E].

Limitations, Open Hypotheses (H3, H4, H6) & Rung-f Hold

Proposed 7-part Compiler Form contract, per-machine Linux RAPL reported_j compile payback, and De Bruijn warm-cache vs. cold-build separation. Dedicated to the public domain under CC0-1.0.

Key Claims & Audited Scope ([T] / [E] / [M] / [S])

  1. [M/S · Proposed Normal-Form Contract, Not a principle of Nature] The primary paper explicitly refutes the hypothesis that existing compilers obey a single "Unified Compiler Rule," restating it as a proposed 7-part engineering contract (R, L, C, K, U, E, G) and disclosing in Appendix A that 38 of 55 audited external claims rested on [S]/[K] snippet checks (14 partly overstated, 4 contradicted, 17 not found).
  2. [E · Per-Machine Cold Prelude & Optimization Payback (reported_j)] Across 20 integer/fixed-point kernels × 15 compiler tiers (300/300 matching checksums), factoring RCE’s emitted Rust runtime into pre-compiled librce_rt.rlib cut median per-kernel rustc -O3 core reported_j 20.07x (56.29 J -> 2.81 J core, 896.93 J -> 27.05 J pkg, 24.58x faster, lowering payback vs. Node JS from 31,080 to 1,079 runs) on AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (Zen 5, pinned CPU 0, co-tenant load on other cores noted), and replicated at 15.44x PP0 core (84.40 J -> 5.47 J, 104.56 J -> 6.85 J pkg = 15.26x) on an idle dedicated Intel Core i9-13900H (4.46 W idle pkg)—while -O2 to -O3 never paid back its extra compile joules on 20%–30% of kernels.
  3. [E · Warm De Bruijn Cache Hit (up to 448.5x) vs. Cold Build] Crediting N. G. de Bruijn (1972) for nameless positional variable indexing (v0 - v1 vs. v1 - v0), E5-Scale (245 base programs, 500 verified semantic mutants, 29,890 cross-program pairs) recorded 0 / 500 false hits (whereas naive identifier-stripping collided on 150 / 150 (100%) variable-swap bugs) and cut rebuild work up to 448.5x (1.166 J -> 2.60 mJ rustc -O3 core reported_j) and 167.8x (0.682 J -> 4.07 mJ clang -O3) strictly on warm cache hits over alpha-renamed single-file kernels (66.7%–69.2% rename hit rate; 1.0x on cold unseen builds).

Methods, Baselines, Sample Sizes (N) & Licensing Scope

  • Hardware & Telemetry: (1) E4-Energy / E4-Prelude / E5-Scale: AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (Zen 5, 32 logical CPUs, pinned CPU 0, Linux RAPL core + pkg reported_j; co-tenants present on non-pinned cores); (2) Wave 5 idle replication: dedicated Intel Core i9-13900H (Raptor Lake, 4.46 W idle pkg, Linux RAPL PP0 + pkg reported_j); (3) E5 Wasm/object key study: Intel Xeon @ 2.80 GHz (Ubuntu 24.04.5, clang 18.1.3, rustc 1.97.0, unmetered hash comparison). measured_j = null (board_metered = false).
  • Workload & Suite: E1: cross-directory/rename byte reproducibility; E4-Energy: 20 self-contained integer/fixed-point kernels × 15 C/Rust/Wasm/JS/Python tiers (300 cells); E5: 360 x86-64 objects, 144 Mach-O objects, 288 Wasm objects, 288 linked Wasm modules (26,208 cross-kernel pairs, 9,328 IR mutations); E5-Scale: 185 W1 RCE Forms + 60 C/Rust/Python kernels + 500 verified semantic mutants.
  • Baselines Compared: Raw SHA-256 source/command hash (ccache-style), comment/whitespace-stripped hash, naive AST identifier-stripping (ID - ID), and De Bruijn positional canonicalization (de Bruijn 1972, Maziarz et al. PLDI 2021); inlined RCE Rust prelude vs. pre-compiled librce_rt.rlib.
  • Runs (N) & Uncertainty / Spread: E4: 20 kernels (medians and per-kernel payback distributions reported; 20%–30% of kernels never recover -O2 -> -O3 compile energy; R^2 = 0.9999 for power × time vs. 0.1154 for static Wasm IR size). E5-Scale: deterministic over 245 programs, 29,890 pairs, and 500 mutants.
  • Cold vs. Warm Caching Scope: Explicitly separated: 448.5x (rustc -O3), 167.8x (clang -O3), and 17.15x (rce check+emit) apply only on warm De Bruijn cache hits (69.2% hit rate on 185 renamed RCE Forms; 66.7% on 60 renamed C/Rust/Python kernels). Cold first-time builds pay 100% of compiler cost plus 2.60–4.59 mJ canonicalizer overhead.
  • Artifact & License Status: Kernels, mutant generators, and E4/E5 scripts public in openIE-dev/openie-research-experiments and openIE-dev/rce (Apache-2.0); self-checked by OpenIE, open for independent replication.

From Refuted "principle" to Proposed Normal-Form Contract & Lineage

The manuscript opens by testing—and refuting—the claim that real compilers (gcc, clang, rustc, Go, GHC, XLA, CompCert) already satisfy a unified "Unified Compiler Rule" [E, S]. Instead, it defines a proposed 7-part Compiler Form contract (Representation R, Lowering L, Cost C, Checker K, Reuse U, Energy E, Gate G). Nameless positional variable indexing in R directly applies N. G. de Bruijn (1972) lambda-calculus indices and Maziarz et al. (PLDI 2021) alpha-equivalent IR hashing, sitting alongside incremental build systems such as ccache, Bazel, Adapton (Hammer et al., PLDI 2014), and Rust’s Salsa query engine [S].

Per-Machine Compile Payback (Zen 5 vs. Core i9-13900H) & Warm-Cache Scope

  • Cold compile amortization (E4-Energy & E4-Prelude) [E]: Lowering Python to clang -O3 requires a median of 2,490 executions to pay back compilation joules; stepping from -O0 to -O3 requires 53,464 to 102,720 runs; and -O2 to -O3 never pays back on 20%–30% of the 20 kernels. Pre-compiling RCE’s shared runtime into librce_rt.rlib cut per-kernel rustc -O3 compile energy 20.07x (56.29 J -> 2.81 J core reported_j) on AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (Zen 5) and 15.44x (84.40 J -> 5.47 J PP0 reported_j) on an idle dedicated Intel Core i9-13900H [E].
  • Why De Bruijn positions beat naive ID-stripping (E5-Scale) [E]: Naive identifier stripping (x - y -> ID - ID) falsely collided on 150 / 150 (100%) variable-swap bugs (30.0% false-hit rate overall), whereas De Bruijn slot numbering (v0 - v1 vs. v1 - v0) yielded 0 / 500 mutant collisions and 0 / 29,890 cross-program collisions. On best-case warm cache hits when rebuilding alpha-renamed single-file kernels on pinned CPU 0, De Bruijn lookup (2.60–4.07 mJ) avoided 1.166 J rustc -O3 (448.5x) and 0.682 J clang -O3 (167.8x) rebuilds [E].

  • Debug-path & comment misses (E5 & E5-Scale) [E]: Linked Rust Wasm modules missed on 9/96 two-directory and renamed pairs at opt-level=0/1 because embedded panic column/path strings differed in the data segment; similarly, raw rce fmt nameless preserves # comments unless stripped prior to hashing (128/185 = 69.2% alpha-rename hit rate) [E].
  • Single-file integer scope & [S]/[K] citation limits: E4/E5-Scale cover single-file integer/fixed-point kernels without multi-TU C++ headers, LTO, or GPU shaders; and Appendix A flags 38/55 background literature claims as snippet-level checks requiring primary-text verification (§9) [S].
