Proposed rce-vc v0.1.0 prototype (openIE-dev/rce-vc@aba99fce): 100,000-unit trie admission reported_j, rename handling, and structural collision caveats. Dedicated to the public domain under CC0-1.0.

Key Claims & Audited Scope ([T] / [E] / [M] / [S])

  1. [M/E · Proposed Prototype Contract, Not a physical principle] rce-vc (v0.1.0, 49 offline tests across 6 Rust crates at aba99fce) is a proposed structural repository admission contract, not a principle of nature—and was not benchmarked head-to-head on conflict-resolution precision/recall against git merge-ort, GumTree, Spork, or Mergiraf (Merge-Bench / CONGRA) in this study (§9).
  2. [E · Apple M5 Max L3 reported_j with Spread] Admitting a single unit change into a 100,000-unit persistent 16-way Merkle trie (O(log_16 U) path copy, re-checking only affected dependents) took 69.69 us (min–max 63.5–84.1 us) and 365.35 uJ (346.4–395.7 uJ, N = 5 trials of 320 admissions), or 73.56 us (69.3–75.7 us) and 317.21 uJ (278.9–369.0 uJ, N = 3 sustained trials of 32,000 admissions) in Darwin L3 ri_energy_nj reported_j.
  3. [M/E · Renames vs. Name-Free Key Collisions] Because rcevc-keys hashes normalized de Bruijn token bodies (SHA-256 over "rcevc/unit/v1", positional body, and dependency keys), renaming a function updates its parent slot binding (name-only equivalence) without changing key(u)—however, two distinct functions with identical normalized structure and dependencies (such as f(x, y) = x + y and g(a, b) = a + b in untyped code) collide onto the exact same key(u), remaining separate in the parent directory trie only via named slot bindings while sharing conflict-reuse keys if edited identically.

Methods, Baselines, Sample Sizes (N) & Licensing Scope

  • Hardware & Telemetry: Apple M5 Max (128 GB, macOS 27.2.1, proc_pid_rusage ri_energy_nj L3 reported_j; board_metered = false, measured_j = null). Internal est_uj cost-table placeholders (424–439 mJ) were ~1,200x higher than measured L3 reported_j and are kept strictly separate.
  • Workload & Suite: 49 offline Rust unit/property tests (rcevc-{types,keys,trie,merge,git,cli}: RCE Form, Rust, Python, JSON splitters, merge commutativity, replay determinism) plus synthetic 100,000-unit single-admission microbenchmarks.
  • Baselines Compared: Whole-repository linear re-hashing/re-checking (O(U)) vs. 16-way Merkle path copy + reverse-dependency closure (O(log_16 U + |affected|)). External baseline: not benchmarked head-to-head against git merge-ort, Mergiraf, or Spork on public conflict corpora in this study.
  • Runs (N) & Uncertainty / Spread: N = 5 trials × 320 admissions (mean 69.69 us [63.5–84.1 us], mean 365.35 uJ [346.4–395.7 uJ]); N = 3 sustained trials × 32,000 admissions (mean 73.56 us [69.3–75.7 us], mean 317.21 uJ [278.9–369.0 uJ]).
  • Cold vs. Warm Caching Scope: Content-addressed CAS + conflict-resolution store keyed by canonical unordered conflict signature (base_key, {side_keys}): exact recurring conflict shapes reuse verified resolutions, whereas novel semantic conflicts require human/proposer resolution.
  • Artifact & License Status: Apache-2.0 public repository at https://github.com/openIE-dev/rce-vc (commit aba99fce); self-checked by OpenIE, open for external inspection and replication.

How rce-vc Compares Conceptually to Git (merge-ort), AST Merge, and CRDTs

Git’s merge-ort engine performs fast 3-way line-diff merging with heuristic file-rename detection (50% similarity index) and zero semantic gate checking: two branches that rename or edit adjacent declarations can merge cleanly at the text level while breaking compilation or behavioral invariants [S]. Syntax-aware tools like GumTree (Falleri et al., ASE 2014), JDime / Spork (Larsén et al., 2022), and Mergiraf lift merging from lines to ASTs, while CRDTs (Shapiro et al., 2011) and Darcs/Pijul patch algebras guarantee algebraic convergence without type/test soundness [S]. rce-vc explores a complementary point: indexing top-level semantic units in a 16-way Merkle trie and requiring a declared admission gate (G0 parse -> G1 typecheck -> G2 tests/trace) before advancing a ref [E].

Rename Handling vs. Structural Key Collisions (f(x,y)=x+y vs. g(a,b)=a+b)

Critique #12 asked how name-free de Bruijn unit keys handle renames and structurally identical functions. In rce-vc (§3–§4) [E, M]:

  • Pure renames: Parent module nodes map slot_name -> (key(u), content_digest(u)). Renaming calc_tax to compute_tax moves the slot binding while key(u) stays invariant, enabling rce-vc to verify a name-only refactor by checking multiset equality of unit keys without re-running downstream unit tests [E].
  • Structural collision hazard on identical bodies: Because key(u) strips parameter and self names, two distinct functions in the same project with identical normalized token bodies and dependency keys—for example def add_meters(x, y): return x + y and def add_seconds(a, b): return a + b in untyped Python—produce the exact same key(u) [M, E]. While the parent module trie keeps both named slots (add_meters and add_seconds) distinct via content_digest (H(body, dep_names)), unit-key-indexed caches deduplicate them onto one node, and same-body helper functions without distinct return/unit types cannot be told apart by key(u) alone [M].

Limitations & Unbuilt Milestones (§9)

  • No external merge-conflict benchmark yet: Replay evaluation against git merge-ort, Spork, and Mergiraf on real open-source merge histories (Merge-Bench, CONGRA) is an unexecuted milestone [E].
  • Prototype scope gaps: Cross-file Rust/Python dependency extraction currently resolves intra-file symbol tables only; TypeScript splitting, native Git packfile streaming (gix instead of loose objects), symlinks, executable mode bits, and submodules are not yet implemented in v0.1.0 [E].

Energy & Telemetry Scope

The 317.21–365.35 uJ single-unit admission figure is Apple M5 Max per-process ri_energy_nj (L3 reported_j, measured_j = null), measuring in-memory/CAS Merkle trie updates plus affected-unit checks—not full-project cargo test execution [E].

Key Claims & Audited Scope ([T] / [E] / [M] / [S])

  1. [E · Reconciled Telemetry Class & Both Sides of 7,728x (reported_j)] Earlier metadata paired board_metered = false (measured_j = null) with an unqualified "1.7 mJ" and "> 7,000x" headline. Grounded in GE-H5 (src/content/papers/game-engines.md), both numbers are Intel Core i9-13900H Linux intel-rapl:0 socket reported_j over 500 ticks of N = 10,000 Q32.32 fixed-point actors: compiled C++20 (clang++ -O3) used 1.694 mJ/tick (0.0583 ms/tick, p99 = 0.0654 ms), Wasm32 (Node V8) used 2.211 mJ/tick (0.0724 ms), and Rust -O3 used 3.673 mJ/tick (0.1248 ms), compared against boxed interpreted rce emit python (CPython 3.14) at 13,090.57 mJ/tick (13.09 J/tick, 564.58 ms/tick)—a 7,728x (C++20) and 3,564x–7,728x speedup/energy cut over interpreted Python, not over commercial C++/C# engines (Unity Burst/DOTS, Unreal, Godot).
  2. [E · 32/32 Cross-Architecture Lockstep Parity] Replacing IEEE-754 floats (whose FMA contraction, x87/SSE rounding, and transcendental libraries diverge across chips) with Q32.32 fixed-point integer Forms yielded 0 state-hash divergences across 100,000 ticks in all 32 cells (8 target languages × 4 architectures: macOS arm64, Linux aarch64, Linux x86-64, Windows x86-64) in GE-H1.
  3. [E · Scope Boundary: State Logic Only, Not Rendering or Mesh Physics] Benchmarks step pure deterministic gameplay/kinematic state transitions; GPU rasterization/raytracing, triangle-mesh broadphase/narrowphase collision, audio mixing, and multithreaded ECS job stealing remain outside scope.

Telemetry & Frame-Budget Scope Note: The primary game-engines study (GE-H1 through GE-H4 and GE-H6 through GE-H9) is an unmetered cross-OS determinism and pixel-tolerance investigation (measured_j = null, board_metered = false) citing external 16.67 ms / 20 ms frame-budget orders of magnitude (such as GameRule's 65 µs/actor 308-actor 20 ms ceiling [S]). In GE-H5, the 1.694 mJ/tick vs. 13,090.57 mJ/tick (7,728x) Intel Core i9 Linux RAPL reported_j ratio measures compiled C++20 -O3 against boxed interpreted CPython 3.14 emitted from the same Form — never against native commercial C++/C# engines (Unity, Unreal, Godot).

  • Hardware & Telemetry: GE-H5 10k-actor scaling: Intel Core i9-13900H Linux powercap intel-rapl:0 socket L2 + core PP0 reported_j (measured_j = null, board_metered = false). GE-H1 100k-tick parity: Apple Silicon (ri_energy_nj L3 0.073–13.60 J), Linux x86-64 (RAPL 1.89–181.87 J), Linux aarch64, and Windows x86-64.
  • Workload & Suite: GE-H1: 100,000-tick deterministic arena state machine emitted to 8 targets (C++20, Rust, Zig/C, Go, Wasm32, JavaScript, Scala/JVM, Python). GE-H5: N = 10,000 Q32.32 fixed-point bouncing/interacting actors stepped for 500 ticks.
  • Baselines Compared: Compiled native/Wasm RCE emitters (C++20 -O3, Wasm32, Rust -O3) vs. reference interpreted rce emit python (CPython 3.14); floating-point cross-compiler drift probe vs. Q32.32 integer arithmetic. External commercial game engines (Unity, Unreal, Godot, Bevy): not benchmarked in GE-H5.
  • Runs (N) & Uncertainty / Spread: GE-H1: 32 language×host cells × 100,000 ticks (0 bit mismatches). GE-H5: 500 consecutive ticks at N = 10,000 actors (C++20 mean 0.0583 ms/tick, p99 = 0.0654 ms, 1.694 mJ/tick socket / 1.454 mJ core reported_j).
  • Cold vs. Warm Caching Scope: Warm in-memory tick loop (V8 JIT warmed prior to Wasm32/JS steady-state window; zero cross-tick memoization since actor positions mutate every tick).
  • Artifact & License Status: Core emitters public in openIE-dev/rce (Apache-2.0); benchmark tables and primary paper (CC0-1.0) at research.openie.dev/papers/game-engines/; self-checked, not externally peer-reviewed.

Reconciling joules = null Metadata with 1.694 mJ/tick and 7,728x

In OpenIE’s manuscript frontmatter, board_metered: false indicates measured_j = null (no physical inline DC shunt or wall wattmeter was attached), not the absence of on-chip CPU counters. Setting this post’s energyClass explicitly to reported_j and naming both sides of the ratio removes all ambiguity [E]:

  • Numerator (13,090.57 mJ/tick, 564.58 ms/tick): Reference rce emit python running on CPython 3.14, which allocates boxed Python int objects on every Q32.32 fixed-point multiply-shift across 10,000 actors [E].
  • Denominator (1.694 mJ/tick socket / 1.454 mJ core, 0.0583 ms/tick): Unboxed int64_t C++20 (clang++ -O3) generated from the exact same RCE Form, achieving a 7,728x lower socket reported_j (5,921x for Node V8 Wasm32 at 2.211 mJ/tick; 3,564x for Rust -O3 at 3.673 mJ/tick due to extra bounds/struct-copy checks in the emitted Rust projection) [E].

This 7,728x figure therefore measures the interpreter boxing tax removed by multi-target native codegen, not a speedup over handwritten C++ or Unity Burst/DOTS [E].

Deterministic Lockstep & Replay Verification (GE-H1)

Multiplayer rollback netcode (GGPO) and simulation replay require identical state hashes from identical input logs across heterogeneous client CPUs (arm64 Apple/Snapdragon vs. x86-64 AMD/Intel, browser Wasm32 vs. native server) [S]. By banning hardware-dependent IEEE-754 rounding from core transition Forms and compiling one Q32.32 specification across 8 targets, all 32 host×language combinations produced identical SHA-256 state digests after 100,000 steps [E].

Limitations & Unbenchmarked Subsystems

  • Not a full game engine: A production engine spends most frame power in GPU shader execution, VRAM bandwidth, skeletal animation, GJK/EPA convex-hull collision, and spatial audio—none of which are modeled in 10,000-actor 2D/kinematic state stepping [E].
  • Single-threaded step: Multi-core data-oriented ECS schedulers (Bevy, Flecs, Unity DOTS) and SIMD AVX2/NEON vectorization of emitted loops remain open work [E].

Energy & Telemetry Scope

All joule values are Linux intel-rapl:0 (L2) and macOS ri_energy_nj (L3) reported_j (measured_j = null, board_metered = false), compared strictly within the Intel Core i9-13900H GE-H5 run.

An unmetered architectural framing paper using "Three-Body" strictly as a structural metaphor for separating Specifications, Proposers, and Deterministic Gates—not celestial mechanics.

Signed Provenance · Self-Checked (human_in_gate = false; automated build, benchmark, and proof-checking scripts ran without manual override — not externally peer-reviewed; see Verification & AI-Use Disclosure and Epistemic Glossary).

Canonical Post-Review Essay (rel="canonical"): https://blog.openie.dev/posts/three-body/

Canonical Artifact ID: blake3:tv:16e4e4b439081a0ed33c49753fe852f5ef4a4ac5f32d4bdf70826f08da0e7738 · Evidence Tags: [M] · [S] · Telemetry Class: unmetered

Structural design metaphor separating Specification, Proposer, and Deterministic Gate roles (unmetered framing paper; not celestial mechanics). Dedicated to the public domain under CC0-1.0.

Key Claims & Audited Scope ([T] / [E] / [M] / [S])

  1. [M · Explicit Metaphor Disclosure] "Three-Body" in this essay is a naming metaphor for three interacting software roles (Specification, Candidate Proposer, Deterministic Gate); it invokes no equations or chaos proofs from Poincaré/Newtonian gravitational three-body mechanics.
  2. [M/S · Architectural Separation] Coupling specification intent and acceptance authority inside a single stochastic generator makes silent drift undetectable; isolating an executable gate (tests, typechecker, SAT/SMT, or proof kernel) turns stochastic generation into bounded trial-and-check.
  3. [S · Cross-Study Scope] This paper performs zero new empirical runs (joules = null, unmetered); concrete falsifiers and failure modes of imperfect specifications (such as Goodharting weak test suites) are evaluated in companion studies (gates, deterministic-null, and rce-jepa).

Methods, Baselines, Sample Sizes (N) & Licensing Scope

  • Hardware & Telemetry: Unmetered (joules = null, board_metered = false). Conceptual software-architecture and interface-contract synthesis.
  • Workload & Suite: No empirical benchmark suite executed in this manuscript; analyzes role separation across specification-proposer-verifier pipelines.
  • Baselines Compared: Qualitative comparison against two-party human-prompt-to-LLM commit loops and unverified multi-agent natural-language debate.
  • Runs (N) & Uncertainty / Spread: Not applicable (N = 0 empirical trials in this framing paper; quantitative claims reside in companion empirical papers).
  • Cold vs. Warm Caching Scope: Conceptual discussion only: notes that gated outputs can be indexed for exact recall only while the specification hash remains unchanged.
  • Artifact & License Status: Public-domain essay text (CC0-1.0) on research.openie.dev and blog.openie.dev; no proprietary code required.

Problem, Scope & Metaphor Disclosure

Upfront scope note: the title phrase "Three-Body" is used strictly as a structural software metaphor for a triad of distinct engineering artifacts—(1) Specification, (2) Proposer, and (3) Deterministic Gate—not as an application of gravitational orbital mechanics or Lyapunov chaos theory [M]. Earlier short summaries leaned on physical analogies without stating immediately that this manuscript is an unmetered architectural synthesis (joules = null).

In two-party LLM coding workflows, a human prompt asks a generative model both to interpret an underspecified goal and to judge whether its own patch succeeded [S]. Whenever model weights approximate acceptance checks heuristically, syntax errors, subtle regressions, and hallucinated APIs pass silently into production [S].

Mechanism: Decoupling Proposal Entropy from Gate Soundness

The paper formalizes a classic computer-science separation of concerns in modern agentic pipelines [M, S]:

  • Specification (sigma): Declares typed invariants, postconditions, resource caps, or reference test traces independent of how a candidate solution is found.
  • Proposer (P): Any search mechanism—cached lookup, symbolic solver, small local model, or frontier LLM—free to explore high-entropy candidates without commit authority.
  • Deterministic Gate (G): A reproducible checker (C(z) in {0, 1}) that either admits the candidate with a signed receipt or returns diagnostic counterexamples without mutating protected state [M].

Limitations, Specification Bottlenecks & Failure Modes

  • A gate is only as strong as its specification: As documented in program-repair literature (Qi et al., ISSTA 2015; Wang, Pradel & Liu, ICSE 2026), proposers routinely pass weak or incomplete unit-test gates with overfitting patches that break unstated invariants [S]. Separating the gate prevents gate-bypass bugs, not specification-omission bugs [M].
  • Formal specification authoring cost: Writing complete formal postconditions or mutation-adequate test suites requires upfront human engineering effort (explicitly registered as falsifier RJ-F2 in rce-jepa) [M].
  • Zero standalone empirical data: Readers seeking measured pass rates, counterexample loops, or hardware joules should consult deterministic-null, gates, and rce-jepa rather than treating this framing essay as an experimental proof.

Energy & Telemetry Scope

This study is strictly unmetered (joules = null, board_metered = false). Energy trade-offs between cheap local verification gates and expensive neural proposers are stated analytically as cost-ratio conditions (C_gate << E_proposer) and measured empirically in companion papers.

Epistemic Non-Mixing & Telemetry Ledger

Open Interface Engineering enforces strict non-mixing across physical rail shunts, on-chip counters, datasheet models, and uninstrumented analyses (measured_j $\perp$ reported_j $\perp$ est_j $\perp$ unmetered — cross-class addition or direct cross-tier ratioing is blocked):

  • Hoare (CACM 1969) & Dijkstra (CACM 1975): Pre/postcondition axiomatic semantics and guarded-command program derivation [S].
  • Blum & Kannan (JACM 1995) & Necula (POPL 1997): Designing programs that check their work and Proof-Carrying Code decoupling untrusted producers from small trusted verifiers [S].
  • Qi et al. (Kali, ISSTA 2015) & Wang, Pradel & Liu (ICSE 2026): Empirical demonstrations of test-suite overfitting in automated patch generation and SWE-bench [S].
  • Kambhampati et al. (LLM-Modulo Frameworks, ICML 2024) & Sun et al. (Clover, 2024): Pairing stochastic LLM proposers with external sound verifiers [S].

item.dc:creator: Open Interface Engineering
item.description: Measures parse time, token bloat across 5 tokenizers, and Apple M5 Max per-process ri_energy_nj (reported_j) on a 20,000-record synthetic corpus while reporting 109/170 shared-host IOReport drift rejections.
item.content:encoded:
Measures parse time, token bloat across 5 tokenizers, and Apple M5 Max per-process ri_energy_nj (reported_j) on a 20,000-record synthetic corpus while reporting 109/170 shared-host IOReport drift rejections.

Signed Provenance · Self-Checked (human_in_gate = false; automated build, benchmark, and proof-checking scripts ran without manual override — not externally peer-reviewed; see Verification & AI-Use Disclosure and Epistemic Glossary).

Canonical Post-Review Essay (rel="canonical"): https://blog.openie.dev/posts/ai-reads-human/

Primary Research Paper: https://research.openie.dev/papers/ai-reads-human/

1-Command Replication Kit: https://github.com/openIE-dev/openie-research-experiments/tree/main/replicate · Study Repository: https://github.com/openIE-dev/openie-research-experiments

Canonical Artifact ID: blake3:tv:354d34ae4d1f4445cf393cc82d84c99ac2bac5585366b86e02521716baa3112c · Evidence Tags: [E] · [S] · Telemetry Class: reported_j

Per-record parse and tokenization energy on Apple M5 Max L3 ri_energy_nj (reported_j) plus 109/170 whole-chip IOReport drift rejections. Dedicated to the public domain under CC0-1.0.

Key Claims & Audited Scope ([T] / [E] / [M] / [S])

  1. [E · reported_j, Apple M5 Max ri_energy_nj L3] On 20,000 seeded records (seed = 20261016, CPython 3.13), struct.iter_unpack on a 23 B fixed binary record (using a shared 24-word dictionary) consumed 280.4 nJ/record, vs. 2,212.1 nJ (7.89x) for json.loads, 69,922.1 nJ (249.4x) for C libyaml, 575,799.3 nJ (2,053.8x) for pure-Python PyYAML, and 27,679.2 nJ (98.7x binary / 12.5x json.loads) just to tokenize compact JSON with tiktoken (cl100k_base) before any GPU neural layer runs.
  2. [E · Negative Result 1: Base64/Hex Does Not Save LLM Tokens] Dumping the 23 B binary layout as text for an LLM yielded 20.3 tokens/record in Base64 (0.89x CSV) and 22.7 tokens/record in Hex (0.99x CSV vs. 22.9 for CSV, 36.2 compact JSON, 51.4 YAML, 65.6 pretty JSON)—showing that text-tokenized LLMs do not benefit from binary wire formats unless binary tool payloads bypass the text context window.
  3. [E · Negative Result 2: 109/170 Shared-Host Drift Rejections] Whole-chip IOReport (L2) subtraction failed Falsifier 6 (> 5.0% pre/post idle drift) on 109 of 170 measurement windows on active laptops, motivating worker-subprocess proc_pid_rusage (L3) isolation and leaving inline hardware measured_j and GPU prefill/decode (M4) explicitly open.

Founding Companion Essay: Read alongside the foundational problem statement, The Hidden Energy Crisis at Every Interface.

Methods, Baselines, Sample Sizes (N) & Licensing Scope

  • Hardware & Telemetry: Timing baseline: 8-vCPU Linux Xeon (Python 3.13.5, minimum of 9 repeats; no RAPL exposed). Energy campaign: Apple M5 Max (macOS worker subprocess proc_pid_rusage(RUSAGE_INFO_V6).ri_energy_nj L3 reported_j, alongside audited whole-chip IOReport L2 reported_j; measured_j = null, board_metered = false).
  • Workload & Suite: 34 parse and tokenization workloads over a synthetic seeded 20,000-record corpus (id, 3-word name, float, bool, 3 tags, 31-bit int), plus 5 open tokenizers (cl100k_base, o200k_base, GPT-2, Mistral-7B-v0.1, Qwen2.5-0.5B) and parser-differential hazard checks (Node v20.19.2, jq 1.7, PyYAML 6.0.2, lxml 6.1.3).
  • Baselines Compared: 23 B fixed binary (struct.iter_unpack with shared 24-word table), CSV (RFC 4180), compact/pretty JSON (RFC 8259), C libyaml & pure-Python YAML (1.2.2), XML (lxml), Markdown (CommonMark 0.31.2), and CBOR (RFC 8949). Compiled C/Rust zero-copy parsers (simdjson, Cap’n Proto, FlatBuffers): planned (M8), not yet benchmarked here.
  • Runs (N) & Uncertainty / Spread: Xeon timing: N = 9 repeats over 20,000 records (min reported: 116 ns binary, 904 ns JSON, 85,300 ns libyaml). Apple M5 Max energy: N = 5 windows × 34 workloads = 170 windows (109/170 L2 whole-chip windows flagged for > 5% idle drift; subprocess L3 means reported in parse_energy.tsv).
  • Cold vs. Warm Caching Scope: In-memory buffer parsing after warm-up import; shared 24-word dictionary for the 23 B binary format must be pre-agreed by hash (explicitly noted in Figure 8 so binary byte size is not overstated).
  • Artifact & License Status: Work-in-progress manuscript (CC0-1.0) and full scripts/logs (MIT OR Apache-2.0) in openIE-dev/openie-research-experiments; self-checked, open for external replication.

Problem, Work-in-Progress Scope & Library Caveats

The primary paper explicitly labels itself a work in progress and highlights four methodological boundaries upfront [E]: (1) parsers perform unequal object-allocation work (struct.iter_unpack returns tuples whereas json.loads and PyYAML allocate typed dicts/lists); (2) measurements thus far run inside CPython 3.13 rather than native C++/Rust SIMD parsers (simdjson, serde, FlatBuffers, planned as M8); (3) the 20,000-record corpus is synthetic and identifier-light; and (4) GPU transformer prefill/decode joules (M4) and inline wall-meter measured_j remain unmeasured [E].

Parse Energy, Token Bloat & Parser-Differential Hazards

  • Subprocess ri_energy_nj (L3 reported_j) across formats [E]: Isolating each of the 34 workloads in a fresh macOS worker process resolved a 2,053.8x CPU energy span across the same 20,000 records: 280.4 nJ/rec (struct binary) -> 2,212.1 nJ/rec (json.loads, 7.89x) -> 27,679.2 nJ/rec (tiktoken cl100k_base on compact JSON, 98.7x binary and 12.5x json.loads) -> 69,922.1 nJ/rec (PyYAML + C libyaml, 249.4x) -> 575,799.3 nJ/rec (pure-Python PyYAML, 2,053.8x) [E].
  • Five-tokenizer inflation [E]: Relative to CSV (22.9 cl100k_base tokens/rec), compact JSON uses 36.2 (1.58x), YAML 51.4 (2.24x), and indent-2 JSON 65.6 (2.86x; 2.22x under Qwen2.5 to 3.66x under GPT-2) [E].
  • Interoperability hazards in human-first formats [E, S]: Differential tests confirmed 9007199254740993 (2^53 + 1) parses exactly in Python json while silently rounding to ...992 in Node JSON.parse, duplicate JSON keys behave unpredictably (RFC 8259 §4), and Python json accepts non-standard NaN/Infinity by default [E, S].

Limitations & Negative Results

  • Why 109/170 whole-chip windows were rejected: Unisolated laptop IOReport (L2) drifted by > 5.0% on 109 of 170 runs (64.1%), proving that whole-package subtraction on active workstations cannot reliably resolve microjoule-per-record deltas [E].
  • Binary-as-text fails for LLMs: Encoding the 23 B binary struct into Base64 (20.3 tok/rec) or Hex (22.7 tok/rec) saves almost nothing over CSV (22.9 tok/rec) while destroying legibility—confirming that binary formats help machine-to-machine buses (CBOR, Protobuf), whereas LLM context savings require field projection or grammar-constrained structured decoding [E].

Energy & Telemetry Scope

All joule numbers in this study are macOS kernel proc_pid_rusage (ri_energy_nj, L3 reported_j) CPU-model estimates (measured_j = null, board_metered = false). Background LLM GPU inference figures cited in the paper (3–4 J/output token on 65B LLaMA in Samsi et al. 2023; 0.047 kWh/1,000 generations in Luccioni et al. FAccT 2024 V1.1) are external literature [S], not measurements from this setup.

Epistemic Non-Mixing & Telemetry Ledger

Open Interface Engineering enforces strict non-mixing across physical rail shunts, on-chip counters, datasheet models, and uninstrumented analyses (measured_j $\perp$ reported_j $\perp$ est_j $\perp$ unmetered — cross-class addition or direct cross-tier ratioing is blocked):

  • Provenance Gate: Signed Provenance · Self-Checked (human_in_gate = false)
  • Acquisition Tier: Subprocess On-Chip Counter (reported_j)
  • Telemetry Disclosure: Apple M5 Max subprocess proc_pid_rusage ri_energy_nj L3 reported_j across 20,000 synthetic records (109/170 whole-chip L2 windows rejected for >5% drift).
  • Evidence Class: reported_j (board_metered = false)
  • Catalog Anchor Reading: 2.804e-07 J (reported_j)
  • Sensor / Formula Scope: Apple M5 Max subprocess proc_pid_rusage ri_energy_nj L3 reported_j (280.4 nJ/rec fixed binary vs 2,212.1 nJ JSON & 27,679.2 nJ tiktoken; measured_j = null)

Related Work & Primary Literature ([S])

  • RFC 8949 (CBOR, Bormann & Hoffman 2020) & RFC 8785 (JCS, Rundgren et al. 2020): Standard deterministic binary and canonical JSON wire encodings [S].
  • Protocol Buffers, Apache Avro, Cap’n Proto & Langdale & Lemire (simdjson, VLDB J. 2019): Schema-typed binary serialization and gigabyte-per-second SIMD JSON parsing [S].
  • Willard & Louf (Outlines, 2023), Poesia et al. (Synchromesh, ICLR 2022) & Scholak et al. (PICARD, EMNLP 2021): Finite-state and incremental-parsing constrained decoding for language models [S].
  • Samsi et al. (IEEE HPEC 2023) & Luccioni, Jernite & Strubell (ACM FAccT 2024 V1.1): Empirical GPU energy benchmarks of LLM text generation [S].

Key Claims & Audited Scope ([T] / [E] / [M] / [S])

  1. [S · Dated Primary Retail Archive] Documents exact published prices: HP 9100A desktop calculator at USD 4,900 (1968 brochure), HP-35 at USD 395 (Jan 1972) to USD 195 (early 1975), Micro Computer Industries WordCheck for Commodore PET 32K at USD 200.00 (Compute!, Jan 1981, issue 8, p. 119), Grammatik II at USD 89 (Chicago Tribune, 10 Apr 1988), and Grammatik III at USD 99 (START, Nov 1989), followed by bundling into WordPerfect 3.0 (Alt-F5, Oct 1983), MS Word 2.0 (~1985), WordPerfect 5.2 (Grammatik 5 included, Nov 1992), and Hunspell (USD 0 MPL/GPL/LGPL library license).
  2. [M/S · Narrow Existence Proof, Not Universal Forecast] As stated in §3.2 of the primary paper, spell check proves that some capabilities once sold as standalone "computer intelligence" commoditize to bundled zero price when two conditions hold: near-zero local marginal execution cost and tight complementarity with an existing user surface—it does not prove that open-ended datacenter reasoning will follow the same trajectory.
  3. [S · Global Access Gap] Even bundled local tools reach the ~4.7B–5.5B connected mobile/internet population (GSMA / ITU 2024) rather than all > 7B people, whereas high-price datacenter subscriptions reach a tiny fraction.

Methods, Baselines, Sample Sizes (N) & Licensing Scope

  • Hardware & Telemetry: Unmetered (joules = null, board_metered = false). Primary/secondary archival source reading of vintage magazine advertisements, museum brochures, software chronologies, and ITU/GSMA reports.
  • Workload & Suite: Historical price and bundling timeline across electronic calculators (1968–1975), spreadsheets (1979–1986), and isolated-word spell/grammar checkers (1961–2026).
  • Baselines Compared: Standalone retail software SKUs (WordCheck, Grammatik II/III) vs. bundled host-application features (WordPerfect, Microsoft Word, macOS/iOS/Android system spell services, Hunspell).
  • Runs (N) & Uncertainty / Spread: Archival point quotes with exact source discrepancies preserved rather than smoothed (e.g., Datamath vs. Finseth hpdata dates on HP-35 cuts from USD 395 -> USD 295 -> USD 225 -> USD 195; missing exact month durations explicitly noted in §2).
  • Cold vs. Warm Caching Scope: Algorithmic shift from timeshared PDP-10 (SPELL, 1971) to hashed/affix-compressed RAM dictionaries (McIlroy 1982 ~30,000 words in 64 KB PDP-11 address space; Hunspell affix tries) running locally on every keystroke.
  • Artifact & License Status: Public-domain archival essay (CC0-1.0) at research.openie.dev/papers/spellcheck/; self-checked, not externally peer-reviewed.

Problem, Scope & Why Existence Proofs Differ from Analogies

The primary paper draws a sharp methodological line in §3.2: an analogy claims "AI is like spell check," whereas an existence proof exhibits one completed historical trajectory (Damerau 1964 edit distance -> Gorin 1971 PDP-10 SPELL -> McIlroy 1982 Unix spell -> 1981 USD 200 retail PC disk -> bundled OS keystroke routine) and identifies the exact cost conditions that made bundling inevitable [S, M].

Archival Price Record & Bundling Transition

Every price point in the paper is tied to a specific printed artifact, keeping source gaps explicit [S]:

  • Standalone retail era (1980–1989): Micro Computer Industries advertised WordCheck for dual-disk 32K Commodore PET/CBM systems at USD 200.00 in Compute! (January 1981, p. 119). Reference Software sold standalone grammar/style checkers Grammatik II at USD 89 (Chicago Tribune, April 1988) and Grammatik III at USD 99 (START, November 1989) [S].
  • Absorption into editors and OS layers (1983–present): WordPerfect 3.0 bound Spellcheck to Alt-F5 inside its USD 495 word processor (October 1983); Microsoft Word 2.0 bundled a licensed Software Heaven dictionary (~1985, per Richard Brodie); WordPerfect 5.2 absorbed Grammatik 5 (November 1992) weeks before acquiring Reference Software (January 1993); and Hunspell removed separate licensing fees across LibreOffice, Firefox, Chrome, and macOS [S].

Limitations & Non-Generalizability Caveats

  • Isolated-word checking vs. context-dependent synthesis: Kukich (1992) separated nonword detection and isolated-word correction from context-dependent semantic/discourse repair. Only the first two fit in kilobyte affix tables at near-zero marginal cost; context-heavy rewriting still invokes larger statistical models [S].

Audits enterprise AI coding TAM projections, reconciles API tokens (~0.75 words/token) and the 1,400-1,481 active-hour assumption behind ~USD 10k/yr spend, and contrasts +21%-55.8% speedups against METR -19% slowdowns.

Signed Provenance · Self-Checked (human_in_gate = false; automated build, benchmark, and proof-checking scripts ran without manual override — not externally peer-reviewed; see Verification & AI-Use Disclosure and Epistemic Glossary).

Canonical Artifact ID: blake3:tv:69e7a2fe33716674a0c355af3726928fd2147ec38c6f5f2e34db059289735979 · Evidence Tags: [M] · [S] · Telemetry Class: unmetered

Exact API token-pricing arithmetic (100k in + 10k out tokens = USD 2.25/query), ARR/spend disclosures, and mixed productivity RCTs (unmetered). Dedicated to the public domain under CC0-1.0.

Key Claims & Audited Scope ([T] / [E] / [M] / [S])

  1. [S/M · Exact Token-vs-Word & Annual Spend Arithmetic] Earlier blog prose blurred API tokens with English words (1 token ≈ 0.75 words, so 100,000 input + 10,000 output tokens ≈ 75,000 + 7,500 words). Under Appenzeller & Li’s (a16z, Oct 2025) frontier pricing example (100k input tokens @ USD 15/M = USD 1.50 + 10k output tokens @ USD 75/M = USD 0.75 = USD 2.25/query), reaching USD 9,450/developer/yr (~USD 10,000/yr) requires 3 queries/hr × 7 active hr/day × 200 days/yr = 4,200 heavy queries/yr (1,400–1,481 intensive active hours/yr, or multi-agent background loops burning ~1,000x chat token volume per Bai, Huang & Wang 2026).
  2. [S · Realized Spend vs. Trillion-Dollar TAMs] Contrasts top-down projections—Appenzeller & Li (a16z, 2025) (30M developers × USD 100k = USD 3T) and McKinsey (2023) (USD 2.6T–4.4T across 63 GenAI use cases)—against realized benchmarks: Menlo Ventures (Dec 2025) (USD 4.0B enterprise AI coding spend out of USD 37B GenAI), Mordor Intelligence (2026) (USD 9.35B rising toward USD 29.96B), Cursor (> USD 1B ARR, Nov 2025), Anthropic (> USD 2.5B Claude Code ARR within USD 14B total ARR, Feb 2026), and Microsoft Form 10-Q (USD 4.1B Q3 2025 pre-tax equity-method loss from OpenAI).
  3. [S · Mixed Productivity RCTs, Including Negative Results] Controlled trials disagree sharply by task familiarity and codebase complexity: Peng et al. (2023) found +55.8% speed on one standalone HTTP server exercise; Paradis et al. (2024) found ~21% faster task completion across 96 Google engineers; whereas METR / Becker, Rush, Barnes & Rein (arXiv:2507.09089, 2025) found 16 experienced open-source maintainers were 19% slower across 246 real issues in their own mature repositories—even though participants believed AI had sped them up by 20%.

Methods, Baselines, Sample Sizes (N) & Licensing Scope

  • Hardware & Telemetry: Unmetered (joules = null, board_metered = false). Primary-source audit of SEC filings, vendor ARR announcements, VC enterprise surveys, API rate cards, and randomized controlled developer studies.
  • Workload & Suite: Published coding-agent token consumption studies (SWE-bench Verified 8-model audit in Bai, Huang & Wang 2026) and three randomized developer productivity trials (Peng et al. 2023, Paradis et al. 2024, Becker et al. 2025).
  • Baselines Compared: Unassisted human software engineering vs. chat/IDE autocomplete vs. autonomous multi-turn coding agents; list-price uncached API billing vs. prompt-cached and Epoch AI (~13x/yr, range 9x–900x/yr) falling per-token prices.
  • Runs (N) & Uncertainty / Spread: Literature RCT sample sizes & intervals: Peng et al. (N = 95 developers, +55.8%), Paradis et al. (N = 96 Google engineers, ~21% speedup), METR / Becker et al. (N = 16 maintainers, 246 real tasks, -19% slowdown); Bai et al. (8 models, ~1,000x token multiplier vs. chat, 30x same-task token spread without accuracy gain).
  • Cold vs. Warm Caching Scope: Explicitly notes that provider prompt-prefix caching (50%–90% input discount on repeated repository context) and falling per-million-token prices (~13x/yr, Epoch AI) pull per-query cost down, while autonomous retry/test loops push token volume up.
  • Artifact & License Status: Public-domain market & literature audit (CC0-1.0) at research.openie.dev/papers/ai-coding-market/; self-checked, not externally peer-reviewed.

Token-vs-Word Correction & Exact USD 10,000/Year Arithmetic

In subword BPE tokenizers (cl100k_base / o200k_base), 100,000 API tokens correspond to roughly 75,000 English words (or ~2,500–3,500 lines of source code), not 100,000 words [S]. Reproducing the exact arithmetic from Appenzeller & Li (Andreessen Horowitz, October 2025) makes every assumption transparent [S, M]:

  • Single heavy agent turn: 100,000 input tokens at USD 15.00 / 1M (USD 1.50) plus 10,000 output tokens at USD 75.00 / 1M (USD 0.75) equals USD 2.25 per query (before prompt-cache discounts) [S].
  • Annualized intensive single-seat schedule: 3 queries/hour × 7 active coding hours/day × 200 workdays/year = 4,200 queries/year (1,400 intensive active hours/year) × USD 2.25 = USD 9,450/developer/year (reaching USD 10,000/yr at ~4,444 queries / ~1,481 hours, or at far fewer human hours when multi-agent background loops issue dozens of autonomous sub-calls per ticket) [S, M].

Enterprise Spend Disclosures vs. Agentic Token Inflation

  • Surveyed spend and vendor ARR [S]: Menlo Ventures (December 2025) estimated enterprise AI coding spend at USD 4.0B (the largest vertical inside USD 37B enterprise GenAI spend), alongside Mordor Intelligence (2026) (USD 9.35B market size projected to USD 29.96B), Cursor (> USD 1.0B ARR, November 2025), and Anthropic (> USD 2.5B annualized Claude Code run-rate inside USD 14B total ARR, February 2026), while Microsoft’s Q3 2025 Form 10-Q disclosed a USD 4.1B pre-tax equity-method loss attributable to OpenAI [S].
  • Price deflation vs. volume explosion [S]: While Epoch AI documents ~13x/year (9x–900x/yr across tiers) declines in constant-capability inference prices, Bai, Huang & Wang (arXiv:2604.22750, 2026) measured 8 coding models on SWE-bench Verified and found agentic loops burn ~1,000x more tokens than single-turn chat, with up to 30x token variance on the exact same bug without higher solve rates [S].

Mixed Developer Productivity RCTs (Including the METR -19% Slowdown)

Any honest economic assessment must report that randomized developer productivity trials do not show uniform speedups [S]:

  • Greenfield / bounded corporate tasks: Peng et al. (2023) measured a +55.8% speedup (N = 95) on a self-contained JavaScript HTTP server task, and Paradis et al. (2024) measured ~21% faster completion (N = 96 Google engineers) on internal enterprise tasks [S].
  • Experienced maintainers on mature codebases (METR 2025): Becker, Rush, Barnes & Rein (arXiv:2507.09089, 2025) randomized 246 real issues across 16 seasoned open-source maintainers working in large repositories they already knew intimately: AI-allowed tasks took 19% longer due to prompt iteration, reviewing plausible-looking errors, and context mismatch, despite developers perceiving a 20% speedup [S].

Energy & Telemetry Scope

An unmetered microeconomic and information-theoretic cost model comparing ambiguous natural-language handoffs against typed, deterministically verified interfaces.

Key Claims & Audited Scope ([T] / [E] / [M] / [S])

  1. [M · Analytical Cost Model, unmetered] Models handoff cost as the sum of upfront specification cost C_spec, serialization/channel work C_chan, boundary verification C_gate, and probability-weighted downstream failure remediation p_err L_downstream—showing analytically that typed deterministic gates dominate when C_spec + C_gate < Delta p_err L_downstream.
  2. [M · Regime Reversal When Exploration Dominates] Explicitly identifies the counter-regime: on one-off exploratory prototypes (N_reuse = 1) with low failure severity (L_downstream small) and fluid requirements, heavy upfront formalization loses to lightweight natural-language iteration.
  3. [S · Classical Institutional Lineage] Connects software API/gate design directly to Coasean transaction costs, Williamsonian incomplete contracts, and Marschak–Radner team theory without claiming empirical field-experiment validation in this paper.

Methods, Baselines, Sample Sizes (N) & Licensing Scope

  • Hardware & Telemetry: Unmetered (joules = null, board_metered = false). Closed-form algebraic cost-accounting propositions and literature synthesis.
  • Workload & Suite: No empirical software or organizational dataset collected in this study.
  • Baselines Compared: Analytical comparison: unverified prose handoffs (C_spec low, p_err high) vs. schema-typed, gate-checked handoffs (C_spec paid once, amortized over N calls).
  • Runs (N) & Uncertainty / Spread: Not applicable (N = 0 empirical runs; hand-derived algebraic inequalities [M], not proof-assistant formalized).
  • Cold vs. Warm Caching Scope: Models amortization over N repeated interface crossings: upfront schema design behaves like compilation, requiring N > N_crit crossings before net savings turn positive.
  • Artifact & License Status: Public-domain manuscript (CC0-1.0) at research.openie.dev/papers/interface-economics/; self-checked, not externally peer-reviewed.

Problem, Scope & Theoretical Boundary

Why do software teams and multi-agent pipelines spend so much effort translating structured state into English prose and parsing it back out? interface-economics treats this question as an unmetered analytical modeling essay ([M], [S]), extending transaction-cost economics (Coase 1937; Williamson 1979) and team information theory (Marschak & Radner 1972) to human-machine and agent-to-agent APIs [S]. No live enterprise RCT or hardware joule meter is run in this paper.

Analytical Trade-Off: Upfront Specification vs. Downstream Remediation

Across a chain of k sequential handoffs where each unverified step admits a subtle interpretation error with probability q, end-to-end survival decays exponentially as (1 - q)^k [M]:

  • Amortized production interfaces (N >> 1, high L_downstream): Paying a fixed schema and verifier cost once collapses q on covered invariants and amortizes C_spec / N toward zero across repeated calls [M].
  • Exploratory one-offs (N = 1, shifting goals): When the human principal does not yet know which product feature to build, rigid formal interfaces lock in premature assumptions and cost more than conversational prototyping [M].

Limitations & Falsifiers

  • Hand-derived stylized parameters: Propositions assume stationary error probabilities and separable specification costs; in real organizations, specification maintenance incurs ongoing versioning overhead whenever upstream requirements drift [M, S].
  • No empirical parameter estimation here: Empirical measurements of prose vs. binary handoff overhead (75,374x Thor measured_j in CTA-E4 and 2,053.8x parse reported_j in ai-reads-human) live in companion engineering studies, not in this economic framing note.

  • Coase (Economica, 1937) & Williamson (Journal of Legal and Economic Studies, 1979): Transaction-cost theory of firm and contract boundaries [S].
  • Marschak & Radner (1972) & Arrow (1974): Economic theory of teams and organizational information channels [S].
  • Parnas (CACM, 1972) & Meyer (IEEE Computer, 1992): Information-hiding module boundaries and Design by Contract [S].

Scope Honesty: Design Specification vs. Shipped Kernel

Operating-system research has a thirty-year history of energy-first resource management—from Odyssey (Flinn & Satyanarayanan, SOSP 1999), ECOSystem (Zeng et al., ASPLOS 2002), and Cinder (Roy et al., EuroSys 2011) to shipping Linux Energy Aware Scheduling (EAS), cpufreq/schedutil, and powercap RAPL [S].   • What is verified today [E]: A 7-crate Rust specification spine (310 tests) enforcing two-phase hold/settle joule-reserve accounting (preventing concurrent child tasks from double-spending a shared battery reserve) and checking 280 × 280 = 78,400 pairs of provenance tags so an analytical est_j (L4) or modeled RAPL (L2, see Schöne et al. 2021 on AMD Zen 2) reading can never silently promote to physical shunt measured_j (L1).

Accelerator capex vs. electricity cost share (74 Epoch AI sites), reconciled 280x -> 70x (~74x) / 141x price decomposition, and SEC capex/OCF audit (unmetered). Dedicated to the public domain under CC0-1.0.

Key Claims & Audited Scope ([T] / [E] / [M] / [S])

  1. [M/S · Corrected 280x Factor Arithmetic] Stanford AI Index ([18]) reports GPT-3.5-equivalent API price fell > 280x over 1.9 years (Nov 2022–Oct 2024), while hardware capex/FLOP improved ~30%/yr (1.98x ≈ 2.0x) and hardware energy efficiency improved ~40%/yr (1.90x ≈ 2.0x). Arithmetic correction: dividing 280x multiplicatively by both ~2x factors gives 280 / (2 × 2) = 70x (~74x using 1.98 × 1.90), not ~140x! In the primary paper’s cost equation, ~141x (280 / 1.98) arises when dividing by the single ~2.0x hardware-capex factor alone because plug electricity is only 1.5%–11.8% of rental cost (so a 1.90x watt-efficiency gain reduces total hourly cost by < 6%, not 2x). Under either accounting, 70x to 141x of the price drop came from software serving, quantization, batching, distillation, and margin compression rather than transistor scaling.
  2. [M/S · Capital Dominates Plug Electricity 8x–70x] Across 74 Epoch AI frontier datacenter sites (median USD 33,300 capex and 880 W per H100-equivalent over 4–6 yr depreciation, 40%–80% utilization, USD 0.04–0.12/kWh), total accelerator cost is USD 0.83–2.50/hr, of which electricity is 1.5%–11.8%—making idle/tail-latency GPU underutilization primarily a capital-destruction problem.
  3. [S · SEC Filing Cash-Flow & Circular-Financing Bounds] Auditing FY2025/FY2026 10-K/10-Q filings shows NVIDIA’s disclosed ecosystem commitments (USD 42B = USD 30B OpenAI + up to USD 10B Anthropic + USD 2B CoreWeave) represent <= 19.5% of FY2026 revenue (USD 215.9B); Alphabet, Meta, Microsoft, and Amazon fund capex out of operating cash flow (0.56x–0.94x OCF), whereas Oracle (1.74x OCF) and CoreWeave (3.37x OCF, 11.8x obligations/revenue, Microsoft 67% of 2025 revenue) carry concentrated debt/lease leverage.

Methods, Baselines, Sample Sizes (N) & Licensing Scope

  • Hardware & Telemetry: Unmetered (joules = null, board_metered = false). Hand-derived M/G/1 and batch-latency cost propositions (Propositions 1–8, [M], not proof-assistant checked) paired with published Epoch AI facility datasets and SEC 10-K/10-Q financial statements ([S]).
  • Workload & Suite: 74 frontier AI cluster records (Epoch AI), Nov 2022–Oct 2024 MMLU >= 60% inference price series (Stanford AI Index), and FY2025/FY2026 filings for NVIDIA, Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Oracle, and CoreWeave.
  • Baselines Compared: Hardware-only cost/efficiency trend (1.98x capex/FLOP; 3.76x–4.0x naive product with 1.90x J/FLOP) vs. observed > 280x API price drop; hyperscaler OCF-funded capex vs. neocloud debt/lease-financed capex.
  • Runs (N) & Uncertainty / Spread: Parameter sensitivity ranges explicitly propagated: 4–6 yr GPU depreciation, 40%–80% utilization, USD 0.04–0.12/kWh electricity -> USD 0.83–2.50/hr total cost and 1.5%–11.8% electricity share.
  • Cold vs. Warm Caching Scope: Analyzes KV-cache memory-capacity ceilings, continuous batching, prefix caching, and speculative decoding as the primary software multipliers behind the 70x–141x non-hardware price decline.
  • Artifact & License Status: Public-domain manuscript and filing ledger (CC0-1.0) at research.openie.dev/papers/latency/; self-checked, not externally peer-reviewed.

Reconciling the 280x Inference Price Decomposition (70x vs. ~141x)

An earlier blog summary wrote that GPT-3.5-level API prices fell 280x while hardware cost and hardware energy efficiency each improved ~2x, yet stated a residual of ~140x—a clear arithmetic slip if both 2x factors are divided out (280 / (2 × 2) = 70x). Checking §12 of src/content/papers/latency.md resolves both numbers cleanly [M, S]:

  • Multiplicative two-factor bound (70x / ~74x): Using Epoch AI’s ~30%/yr price-performance gain (1.30^1.9 ≈ 1.65x–1.98x ≈ 2x) and ~40%/yr energy-efficiency gain (1.40^1.9 ≈ 1.90x ≈ 2x), dividing 280x by both factors yields 70x (280 / 4, or ~74x at 1.98 × 1.90 = 3.76x) [M, S].
  • Why energy efficiency does not halve hourly GPU cost (~141x vs. capex alone): In hourly cost c_hr = a / U + P p_elec, plug power P p_elec is only 1.5%–11.8% of c_hr (USD 0.035–0.106/hr out of USD 0.83–2.50/hr across 74 Epoch AI sites). Cutting watts per FLOP by 1.90x therefore lowers total hourly hardware cost by only ~1%–6%, leaving 280 / 1.98 ≈ 141x unexplained by cheaper hardware alone [M, S].

Under either bound (70x conservative multiplicative or ~141x capex-weighted), software algorithmic serving—continuous batching (vLLM), FP8/INT4 quantization, FlashAttention, speculative decoding, and smaller distilled models—drove roughly two orders of magnitude more price deflation than silicon scaling [S].

Latency SLOs, Utilization & SEC Balance-Sheet Stratification

  • Interactive tail-latency tax (Propositions 1–8) [M]: Tight interactive time-per-output-token (TPOT) and time-to-first-token (TTFT) SLOs cap batch size before compute units saturate, forcing operators to hold spare GPU headroom where amortized capital (8x–70x electricity) burns continuously even while idle [M].
  • Filing-grounded financial risk [S]: Hyperscalers (Alphabet 0.57x, Meta 0.62x, Microsoft 0.65x, Amazon 0.94x capex/OCF) self-finance cluster buildouts from legacy software/search/commerce cash flows, whereas Oracle (1.74x capex/OCF, USD 11.4B customer prepayments inside USD 23.1B OCF) and CoreWeave (3.37x capex/OCF, lease/debt obligations 11.8x revenue, 67% single-customer concentration at Microsoft) carry acute utilization and refinancing sensitivity [S].

Limitations & Scope

  • Hand-derived queuing models: Propositions 1–8 are classical analytical derivations ([M]), not machine-checked Lean theorems.
  • Point-in-time filings: Financial ratios reflect FY2025 / early-FY2026 SEC 10-K and 10-Q disclosures and do not observe private off-balance-sheet SPV terms or confidential enterprise API margin sheets [S].

Key Claims & Audited Scope ([T] / [E] / [M] / [S])

  1. [M/S · Ex-Post Pedagogical Framing vs. Falsifiable Engineering] On avalanche.openie.dev, aligning 24 evolutionary signaling milestones (CL01–CL24, quorum sensing to writing) with 38 AI milestones (AI01–AI38, 1950–2026) across 9 rungs is an ex-post interpretive and educational framing—useful for teaching why stateless tool loops (Rungs 1–5) re-pay inference costs on recurring patterns, not a deductive proof that silicon software must recapitulate biological phylogeny.
  2. [T · Scope of the 45 CTA Lean 4.36.0 Consent Theorems] The 45 theorems in QuorumRatchet.lean, OrchestrationFlow.lean, and EnzymaticSynthesis.lean (part of 132 portal-highlighted 6-kernel theorems) verify an abstract discrete state-machine property—that an agent transition gated by g_i(s_i, m) = 1 rejects unconsented messages—NOT a clinical, neurobiological, or hardware safety guarantee for human brain-computer interfaces.
  3. [E · Finite-Sample Gate Counts & Host Separation] Replaces the portal banner’s shorthand "zero-escape shorthand" with exact finite-sample counts (0 broken commits admitted on 59/60 CTA-E2 tasks, 44/48 MoL tasks, and 29/32 BigCodeBench slice tasks—bounded by sample size N and unit-test coverage, while CTA-E5 DES-10 observed 1 / 100 (1.0%) false commit alongside 98/100 solves!), and separates Thor 927.30 uJ (50.13 us, measured_j) from faster desktop 23.84–29.54 us (reported_j) hosts.

Methods, Baselines, Sample Sizes (N) & Licensing Scope

  • Hardware & Telemetry: Educational Astro portal (openIE-dev/avalanche-openie-web) summarizing primary measurements from communication-avalanche.md (NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor TI INA3221 VDD_CPU_SOC_MSS measured_j + Core i9-13900H / M3 Ultra / Ryzen AI Max+ 395 reported_j) and lut-adapt.md.

  • Baselines Compared: Ten isolated AI paradigm camps (C1 solo LLM 48/100, C9 3-agent NL debate 49/100, C2 SAT/FD 30/100, C8 LUT6/FSM 20/100, C5 Shape D 16/100, C4 MCTS 10–11/100, C7 causal do(X) 10/100, C6/C10 4/100, C3 EBM 0/100) vs. routed DES-10 (98/100).

avalanche.openie.dev was built as an interactive reader companion to communication-avalanche, offering dual "Visionary / Scientist" explanation registers [M]. To prevent the accessible register from overstating what was proved:

  • Interpretive history ([S]/[M]): Grouping quorum sensing (Nealson et al. 1970), slime-mold network pruning (Tero et al., Science 2010), and major evolutionary transitions (Maynard Smith & Szathmáry 1995) alongside 1950–2026 AI architectures is a conceptual lens, not a quantitative principle predicting calendar dates of future AI breakthroughs [S, M].

[S · Three Classical Sciences Placed by Altitude] Synthesizes Information Theory (Shannon 1948 channel/representation bounds; Landauer 1961 physical bit erasure) as the physical substrate, Game Theory (von Neumann & Morgenstern 1944; Nash 1950 equilibria) as strategic interaction over payoffs, and Mechanism Design (Hurwicz, Maskin & Myerson, 2007 Nobel lecture lineage) as rule/gate routing that aligns incentives or proposals with desired outcomes.

[M · Honest Cross-Portal Licensing Boundary] While the stack.openie.dev web guide is openly readable, the eight domain stacks it indexes do not share one blanket software license: rce, rce-vc, deterministic-null, and lut-adapt-ai are Apache-2.0 public repos, whereas JouleDB (data.openie.dev) and Pattern-lang (synthesis.openie.dev) use BSL-1.1 with private core mirrors, and JouleOS remains private.

stack.openie.dev is an architectural map and teaching index, not a research experiment [M]. Key Claims & Audited Scope ([T] / [E] / [M] / [S])

[M/S · Unmetered 7-Axis Epistemic Schema] knowledge.openie.dev specifies a factual claim as claim = ⟨V_t, T_t, R_t, G, S, C, P⟩—requiring three distinct timestamps (Valid Time when true in the world, Transaction Time when recorded in the ledger, and Reference Time when queried), two domain bounds (Granularity and Scope), and two epistemic anchors (Calibrated Certainty and Cryptographic/Source Provenance). Exact bwrap 6-kernel (con-leche, con-ron, lean4lean, nanoda, leanchecker --paranoid, Lean v4.36.0) counts are: 1,264 source declarations (5,393 kernel constants) in rce (0 sorry in completed files, alongside 12 unproved Draft-0.9 theorem statements in Appendix F.9), 58 theorems in lut-adapt, 45 theorems (53 decls) in communication-avalanche, and 31 theorems (50 decls) in time-as-an-index.
  3. [S · Direct Lineage in Bitemporal Databases & Provenance Standards] Connects AI hallucination prevention directly to Snodgrass & Ahn’s bitemporal relational model (SIGMOD 1985 / SQL:2011), W3C PROV-DM (2013), and Wikidata statement qualifiers (Vrandečić & Krötzsch, 2014).

Methods, Baselines, Sample Sizes (N) & Licensing Scope

Training a language model on dated web snapshots compresses millions of time-bound, source-specific statements ("the API rate limit in v2.1 on 2024-05-01 is 100 req/min") into shared floating-point weights where Valid Time, Transaction Time, Scope, and Provenance are lost [M, S]. Extending Snodgrass & Ahn (1985) from bitemporal (V_t, T_t) to tritemporal (V_t, T_t, R_t) plus granularity, scope, conformal calibration (C), and hash/citation provenance (P) separates invariants that belong in compiled logic/weights from transient facts that must be retrieved with axes intact [M, S].

  • Formal axioms != empirical truth: Six proof kernels certify that a theorem follows deductively from its stated Lean definitions; they do not validate physical sensor calibration or real-world market assumptions [M].

Key Claims & Audited Scope ([T] / [E] / [M] / [S])

  1. [M · data.openie.dev Is a 1,260,000-Cell Design Taxonomy, Not a DBMS Benchmark] data.openie.dev classifies storage and retrieval engines along 10 orthogonal axes (⟨W, S, T, C, D, Q, V, R, N, tau⟩ with cardinalities 5 × 12 × 4 × 7 × 5 × 7 × 5 × 4 × 6 × 5 = 1,260,000 discrete cells), and its interactive /instrument animation uses illustrative unit weights (0.4, 1.6, 9, 22), not hardware joule readings.

  3. [S/E · Candid JouleDB Licensing & Missing External DBMS Baselines] Companion product JouleDB (openIE-dev/jouledb) is licensed under BSL-1.1, its full core storage-engine source currently lives in a private internal mirror (the crates.io crate is an installer stub rather than full engine source), and no head-to-head TPC-H, ClickBench, or YCSB joule benchmark against DuckDB, ClickHouse, RocksDB, or PostgreSQL is reported here.

Methods, Baselines, Sample Sizes (N) & Licensing Scope

  • Hardware & Telemetry: DNULLMM1 mmap microbenchmark (rce-jepa): Apple M5 Max (128 GB, macOS proc_pid_rusage ri_energy_nj L3 reported_j; measured_j = null). data.openie.dev taxonomy & browser canvas: unmetered (joules = null).
  • Workload & Suite: 40,000 POSIX mmap exact-digest lookups over a frozen 34-record DNULLMM1 store (sha256: d92a57b4...), paired with the 10-axis combinatoric impossibility pruning analysis on data.openie.dev.
  • Baselines Compared: DNULLMM1 mmap Gear-0 lookup (1.771 uJ reported_j) vs. cold neural repair generation (84.25 J local 35B reported_j in rce-jepa). External DBMS baselines (DuckDB, ClickHouse, SQLite, RocksDB): not benchmarked in this study.

  • Cold vs. Warm Caching Scope: Warm OS page-cached mmap over a tiny (34-record) immutable file; large out-of-RAM NVMe working sets (io_uring / page-fault misses) and write-ahead log fsync costs are not exercised.
  • Artifact & License Status: Taxonomy text (CC0-1.0) on data.openie.dev; DNULLMM1 binary reader (Apache-2.0) in openIE-dev/deterministic-null; JouleDB (openIE-dev/jouledb) is BSL-1.1 with private core mirror and crates.io installer stub — externally unreproduced.

Storage–Query Impedance & Classical Database Energy Literature

The central insight of data.openie.dev—that query cost is governed by storage–workload impedance (the structural distance between physical layout S, such as B-trees, PAX/columnar runs, CSR graphs, or HNSW vectors, and query zone W)—builds directly on *Idreos et al.’s Periodic Table of Data Structures / Data Calculator (SIGMOD 2018) and Stonebraker & Cetintemel’s "One Size Fits All: An Idea Whose Time Has Come and Gone" (ICDE 2005)* [S].

Crucially, classical database energy research established important boundary findings that temper naive hardware claims [S]: Harizopoulos, Shah, Meza & Ranganathan (CIDR 2009) and Tsirogiannis, Harizopoulos & Shah (SIGMOD 2010) showed on enterprise servers that the most time-efficient query plan (e.g., columnar projection or indexed probe over full table scan) is almost always the most energy-efficient database plan because high server idle power makes runtime minimization dominant [S].

Separating DNULLMM1 (34 Records), data.openie.dev, and JouleDB (BSL-1.1)

To remove any impression that 0.325 us / 1.77 uJ represents a general-purpose SQL engine beating modern analytical databases [E]:

  • DNULLMM1 (Apache-2.0 in openIE-dev/deterministic-null): A compact, immutable mmap hash table used as Gear-0 exact-match cache (34 records in the 1.771 uJ M5 Max L3 reported_j test) [E].
  • JouleDB (BSL-1.1 at openIE-dev/jouledb): A commercial/source-restricted database project whose core engine currently resides in a private internal repository (with an installer stub on crates.io). Until public reproducible benchmarks against DuckDB (Raasveldt & Mühleisen, SIGMOD 2019), ClickHouse (Schulze et al., VLDB 2024), and SQLite/RocksDB are published with open harness scripts, JouleDB claims carry zero externally reproduced empirical weight on this blog.

Limitations & Open Benchmarks

  • Tiny RAM-resident mmap table: 34 records fit entirely inside Apple M5 Max L1/L2 CPU cache; cold NVMe random 4 KiB reads (~50–100 us), fsync durability barriers, and vectorized multi-million-row aggregations (DuckDB / ClickHouse) cost orders of magnitude more time and energy [M, S].

Energy & Telemetry Scope

Only the 34-record DNULLMM1 mmap probe (1.771 uJ) is reported_j (Apple M5 Max L3, measured_j = null); data.openie.dev’s 1,260,000-cell map is unmetered.

4 KB CompactLut6Page (sys/lut6-core): upfront 2^6 = 4^3 = 64 naming-motivation disclosure, Thor measured_j, Cortex-M55 DWT cycles, and XC7A200T est_W/est_C. Dedicated to the public domain under CC0-1.0.

Key Claims & Audited Scope ([T] / [E] / [M] / [S])

  1. [M/T · Analogy Label: Counting Parallel, NOT Biological Isomorphism] Upfront clarification (Critique #6): the numerical coincidence between 2^6 = 64 (entries in a 6-input Boolean LUT6 truth table, packed in one uint64 word or Xilinx LUT6 primitive) and 4^3 = 64 (RNA nucleotide triplets) is a combinatorial counting parallel used strictly as naming motivation ("codon", "wobble", "operon", "nucleus")—not a structural or biochemical isomorphism. Biological genetic-code degeneracy is not shown to filter digital sensor noise; what NucleusCodon.lean proves [T] is a standard Boolean Walsh–Hadamard Fourier fact (Linial, Mansour & Nisan 1993): functions invariant across aligned 2-bit blocks (0x0F << 4q) have exact 0 degree-5 and degree-6 Fourier coefficients (vs. 28 high-degree AC energy on a brittle 1u64 << c 1-hot mask).
  2. [E · Strictly Separated Silicon Measurements] On NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor (TI INA3221 VDD_CPU_SOC_MSS, measured_j), lut6-core uses 162.56 nJ/op (5.45 ns, 87.00x CpJ vs. 14,143.46 nJ INT8 Micro-MLP) in vertical bit-sliced mode, 1,935.05 nJ (65.2 ns, 7.31x) scalar, and 8,594.93 nJ (1.65x) on the in-page 672 B Antisym-40 zero-MUL T-MAC fallback; on a live USB-attached Alif Ensemble E3 (OpenMV-AE3 Cortex-M55 @ 400 MHz, board_metered = false), it runs in 684.57 DWT cycles (1.72 us, 173.83x faster than INT8 MLP) scalar and 2.68 cycles/op (6.97 ns) bit-sliced, while fitting 16,400 B (25.06%) of 64 KB SRAM on nRF52832 Cortex-M4F and RV32IMAC (0 float instructions).
  3. [M/E · M.2 XC7A200T Gateware & Thermal Failure Bound (est_j)] Synthesizing (Yosys 0.71+ + license-free openXC7 nextpnr-xilinx closing post-PAR timing at 320.62 MHz on xc7a200tfbg484-2) maps each 4,096 B CompactLut6Page 1:1 into one 36 Kb RAMB36E1 with (72, 64) Hamming SECDED (0 observed silent corruption at BER = 1% in fault simulation vs. 54.56% on INT8 MLP). Analytical DS181/UG475 modeling (est_j, unprobed on physical M.2 rails) projects 0.86 est_W and 55.2 est_C (45 °C ambient, passive heatsink) when external DDR3 is held in reset—and candidly flags thermal failure (95.8 est_C > 85 °C commercial limit) if DDR3 + PCIe x4 is enabled in a 0 LFM bare slot without >= 200 LFM airflow (63.2 est_C).

Methods, Baselines, Sample Sizes (N) & Licensing Scope

  • Hardware & Telemetry: (1) NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor (TI INA3221 ch2 VDD_CPU_SOC_MSS physical DC shunt, measured_j, board_metered = true); (2) Apple M5 Max (L3 reported_j) & AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (RAPL pkg reported_j); (3) Live USB OpenMV-AE3 (Alif E3 Cortex-M55 @ 400 MHz hardware DWT cycle counter, board_metered = false); (4) Numato Aller A7 (Artix-7 XC7A200T-2FBG484C) Verilator 5.054 12,023-cycle co-sim + openXC7 post-PAR .bit + 673-point AMD DS181/UG475 coupled leakage model (est_j / est_C, board_metered = false).
  • Workload & Suite: 4,096 B CompactLut6Page (256 LUT6s + 672 B EntroMCU 1.602 b/w Antisym-40 T-MAC tail), 64/64 Yosys abc -lut 6 Boolean miter vectors, 40 noisy skill paraphrases + 8 OOD abstention probes, BER = 1.0% (10^-2) SEU bit-flip injection, and 10,500 cross-family (XC7A200T vs. XCK26) RTL equivalence vectors.
  • Baselines Compared: 2-layer INT8 (64->32->16) and BF16 Micro-MLPs, unpruned FiniteDiff DWN (64 gates vs. 23 DiffLUT-Net -64.06% and 16 wobble-pruned -75.00%), naive 80-LUT6 Shannon expansion vs. 22-LUT6 Lupanov (-72.5%), and DDR3-active vs. DDR3-tie-off M.2 gateware.
  • Runs (N) & Uncertainty / Spread: Thor shunt: 9-window counterbalanced ABBA harness (bench_lut6_nucleus_shunt.rs). XC7A200T vs. KV260 co-sim: 12,023 cycles / 10,500 vectors (0 bit mismatches). Charon + Aeneas + Lean 4.36.0: 50–58 six-kernel-verified LutAdapt theorems (0 sorry).
  • Cold vs. Warm Caching Scope: Two immutable ROM/MRAM seed pages + two mutable SRAM/DTCM surgical overlay pages: 4-part Means Test refuses unamortized one-off tasks (N = 1 < N_crit = 1.90), unverified guesses (delta < 1.0), and high-entropy prose (H = 4.85 > 1.25 bits), rolling drifted overlays (rej = 3) back to seed (0x3C rollback).
  • Artifact & License Status: Apache-2.0 public code in openIE-dev/lut-adapt-ai (sys/lut6-core/, 15.31 KB lut6_core.wasm) and openIE-dev/openie-research-experiments (aller-a7-xc7a200t/, lut6-core-nucleus/); self-checked, open for external replication.

Naming Motivation vs. Mathematical Content (2^6 = 64 vs. 4^3 = 64)

Why use biological terms (codon, wobble, operon, apoptosis) for a #![no_std] Rust and FPGA lookup-table format? Solely as an intuitive naming mnemonic for a 4,096 B binary page layout [M]:

  • What is merely a counting coincidence: A Xilinx 7-Series/UltraScale+ LUT6 hardware primitive and a 64-bit CPU word (uint64) each hold 2^6 = 64 truth-table bits, matching the cardinality 4^3 = 64 of three-base nucleotide codons. That 64 = 64 equality is not a physical or evolutionary equivalence [M].
  • What is proved mathematically ([T]): In Boolean harmonic analysis (Linial, Mansour & Nisan, JACM 1993), masking or grouping noisy low-order ADC bits so a LUT6 output is constant across 4-state subcubes forces all degree-5 and degree-6 Walsh–Hadamard coefficients to vanish (NucleusCodon.wobble_quartet_high_harmonic_cancels), preventing 1-hot point memorization (0 observed noisy-paraphrase hit rate) and holding 95.00% hit rate (100.0% 40/40 when paired with the in-page 672 B zero-MUL T-MAC tail) [T, E].

Hardware Results Kept Strictly Separate by Substrate

  • NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor (measured_j, physical TI INA3221 shunt) [E]: 162.56 nJ/op (87.00x CpJ vs. INT8 Micro-MLP) vertically bit-sliced; 1,935.05 nJ (7.31x) scalar; 8,594.93 nJ (1.65x) Antisym-40 T-MAC (-49.38% stack SRAM via ISCA 2025 mirror involution T(80 - c) = -T(c), which also flipped AMD Zen 5 RAPL reported_j from 0.68x to 1.12x CpJ over INT8 MLP) [E].
  • Bare-Metal MCU Targets (DWT cycles & static ELF audit, board_metered = false) [E]: Cross-compiles with 0 float instructions across 8 targets (including 15.31 KB wasm32 and 25.06% of 64 KB SRAM on nRF52832 and RV32IMAC), executing in 684.57 cycles (1.72 us) scalar and 10,655.8 cycles (11.17x faster than 119,001.9-cycle INT8 MLP) on live USB-attached Alif E3 Cortex-M55 [E].
  • Artix-7 XC7A200T (Numato Aller A7 M.2 2280, est_j / est_C) [M, E]: Holds 365 4 KB pages on-die (1.46 MB RAMB36E1, 2.53x KV260 BRAM capacity) with (72, 64) SECDED (100 observed accuracy / 0 observed silent corruption at BER = 1% simulated bit flips vs. 26.28% accuracy / 37.0% NaN on BF16 MLP) and closes openXC7 post-route timing at 320.62 MHz [E].

Limitations & Pre-Bench Hardware Gaps

  • M.2 XC7A200T thermal & shunt gap (LA-F30): All XC7A200T watt/Celsius figures (0.86 est_W, 55.2 est_C with DDR3 off; 95.8 est_C bare thermal failure with DDR3 + PCIe x4 at 0 LFM) are analytical est_j/est_C calculations; physical M.2 +3.3 V Kelvin shunt (INA228) and XADC/thermocouple bench probing have not yet been run [M].
  • 6-input locality ceiling: Functions requiring wide global arithmetic without tree/Lupanov decomposition exceed a single 4 KB page and must escalate to T-MAC or neural rungs [M].

Energy & Telemetry Scope

Thor INA3221 (measured_j), M5 Max / Zen 5 (reported_j), Cortex-M55 (DWT cycles), and XC7A200T (est_j) are reported in separate rows and never combined across classes.
